definition_zh: 徒劳的；无用的；无效的；空泛的
definition_en: producing no useful result, or having no chance of success even though effort is made
core_image: 用一只漏底的木桶往井里打水，提上来时只剩几滴水
scene: 洪水退去后，村民们用破桶往田里挑水，来回十几趟，田还是干的。The villagers carried water in broken buckets, but the effort was futile.
sceneCN: 这里 futile 是「徒劳的」（第 1 个义项：付出努力却得不到结果）；句意：村民们用破桶挑水，可这番努力是徒劳的。

pos.zh: 形容词：徒劳的；无用的；无效的；空泛的

derivatives.zh: 由 futile 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「徒劳；无用」
由 futile 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「徒劳地」
由 futile 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「徒劳无益」，比 futility 少见

senses.title: Useless effort
senses.definition: producing no useful result even though real effort is made
senses.definitionCN: 虽然付出了实实在在的努力，却没有产生有用的结果
senses.example: They made a futile attempt to rescue the sinking boat with a broken rope.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用一根断绳去救那条下沉的船，结果只是徒劳。
senses.why: Latin futilis describes a vessel that leaks, so anything poured into it is lost; an effort that cannot hold its result is futile.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 futilis 形容漏水的容器，倒进去的东西都留不住；努力若存不住结果，就是 futile。

senses.title: Pointless because the outcome is fixed
senses.titleCN: 注定无效的；没有意义的
senses.definition: having no chance of success because the result is already settled
senses.definitionCN: 因为结果已经确定，所以没有成功的可能
senses.example: Arguing with the referee after the final whistle was futile.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响之后还和裁判争论，是毫无意义的。
senses.why: Once the vessel cannot hold water, no amount of pouring matters; when an outcome is fixed, further action adds nothing.
senses.whyCN: 容器既然盛不住水，再倒多少也没用；结局已定，后续动作便毫无意义。

senses.title: Trivial and without substance
senses.definition: lacking weight or substance, used of words, gestures, or activities that mean very little
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏分量与实质，用于指意义很小的言语、姿态或活动
senses.example: The meeting dissolved into futile chatter about office furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 会议沦为关于办公室家具的空泛闲聊。
senses.why: The leaky image shifts from effort to content: what is said is like water that runs straight out of the vessel.
senses.whyCN: 漏水的意象从「努力」转到「内容」：说出口的话像水一样从容器里直接流走。

senses.title: Medically without benefit
senses.definition: unable to bring benefit or comfort, used of treatment given when recovery is no longer expected
senses.definitionCN: 无法带来益处或安慰，用于在康复已无望时给予的治疗
senses.example: The family asked whether another round of futile care would only prolong suffering.
senses.exampleCN: 家属问，再做一轮无效治疗是否只会延长痛苦。
senses.why: Modern medicine borrows the word for treatment that cannot restore the patient, so the effort pours into a vessel that will never hold.
senses.whyCN: 现代医学借这个词形容无法让病人恢复的治疗，努力倒进的是一只永远盛不住的容器。

senses.title: Frivolous in character
senses.definition: given to empty display rather than serious purpose, an older literary use
senses.definitionCN: 偏爱空洞的排场而非严肃目的，属于较早的书面用法
senses.example: The court was mocked as a futile place of masks and gossip.
senses.exampleCN: 那个宫廷被讥为只讲面具与闲话的虚浮之地。
senses.why: The oldest figurative sense calls a person or a place futile when it is all surface and no substance, like a jar that holds nothing.
senses.whyCN: 最早的比喻用法把人或场所称作 futile，指只有表面而无实质，如同一只什么都存不住的罐子。

intro.en: Futile comes straight from Latin futilis, a word for a vessel that leaks; the deeper root is disputed, with most dictionaries connecting it to fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: futile 直接来自拉丁语 futilis，本指漏水的容器；更早的词根有争议，多数词典把它与 fundere（倾倒）联系起来。

items.en: Futilis describes a jar or cup that leaks, so that nothing poured into it stays.
items.cn: futilis 形容会漏的罐或杯，倒进去的东西都留不住。

items.en: Classical prose already uses the adjective figuratively for what is worthless or vain.
items.cn: 古典散文已把这个形容词用作比喻，指无价值或徒劳的东西。

items.en: English borrows futile directly from Latin, without a French stage, and applies it to speech and effort.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 futile，没有经过法语阶段，用于言语与努力。

items.en: The word settles into formal prose as the standard adjective for vain effort and hopeless resistance.
items.cn: 这个词在正式散文中固定下来，成为形容白费努力与无望抵抗的常用形容词。

items.en: Medicine, law, and politics extend it to futile care, futile claims, and futile negotiations.
items.cn: 医学、法律与政治把它扩展到无效治疗、无望的诉求与徒劳的谈判。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the words built on futile; the near-meaning group holds other adjectives for effort that comes to nothing.
note.cn: 形近组收由 futile 构成的词；近义组收其他表示「努力落空」的形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being futile, or a useless act or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「徒劳、无用」，也可指徒劳之举，由 futile 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: In a futile manner, without producing a result.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「徒劳地」，由 futile 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being futile, a rarer synonym of futility.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「徒劳无益」，由 futile 加 -ness 构成，比 futility 少见。

entries.definition: Producing no result, often used of hopes and efforts that fail.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「徒劳的、枉然的」，多用于落空的希望与努力。

entries.definition: Yielding nothing useful, used especially of searches and negotiations.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无结果的」，多用于搜寻与谈判。

entries.definition: Without purpose or meaning, plainer and more informal than futile.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无意义的、没有必要的」，比 futile 更口语、更直白。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the leaky-vessel origin, the -ity and -ly family, and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用「漏水容器」这一语源、带 -ity 与 -ly 的词族，以及这个词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Futile comes from a Latin word for a leaking jar: what you pour in runs out again.
normal.cn: futile 来自拉丁语中表示「漏水的罐子」的词：倒进去的东西又会流出来。

normal.en: Futility is the noun, and it names both the quality and the wasted act itself.
normal.cn: futility 是名词，既指「徒劳」这一性质，也指徒劳的行为本身。

normal.en: A futile attempt is one where the effort is real and the result is not.
normal.cn: a futile attempt 指努力是真的、结果却没有的尝试。

normal.en: Prove futile is a common verb phrase: the plan was tried and shown to be useless.
normal.cn: prove futile 是常见的动词搭配：计划试过之后被证明毫无用处。

normal.en: Doctors speak of futile care when treatment cannot restore the patient.
normal.cn: 当治疗无法让病人恢复时，医生会说 futile care。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden bucket with a cracked base and a farmer carrying it up a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一只底上裂了缝的木桶，农夫提着它上山。

abstract.en: Picture a referee blowing the whistle while a player keeps arguing, his words changing nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判已经鸣哨，球员还在争辩，他的话改变不了任何事。

abstract.en: Picture a room where every sentence said aloud drains away like water from a broken cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，说出口的每句话都像破杯里的水一样流走。

examples.en: The rescue was futile because the rope broke before the boat was reached.
examples.cn: 那次救援是徒劳的，因为绳子还没够到船就断了。

examples.en: They argued for hours, but the argument proved futile.
examples.cn: 他们争了几个小时，结果这场争论被证明毫无用处。

examples.en: Constant complaining is a futile habit that changes nothing.
examples.cn: 不停抱怨是一种改变不了任何事的徒劳习惯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费油」——开车绕远路白「费油」，事情还是没办成，就是徒劳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 futilis（漏水的、盛不住水的，引申为「无价值的、徒劳的」）→ 英语 futile。多数词典推测它与拉丁语 fundere（倾倒）有关，但更早的词根存疑；十六世纪英语直接从拉丁语借入，没有经过法语。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses grow from one leaking vessel: effort that yields nothing, action after the outcome is fixed, speech without substance, treatment that cannot heal, and a showy emptiness of character.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从一只漏水的容器长出来：毫无结果可言的付出、结局已定后的动作、没有实质的言语、无法治愈的治疗，以及性格上的虚浮空洞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cracked wooden bucket lifted from a well with almost no water in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只裂了缝的木桶从井里提上来，里面几乎没有水。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: work is poured in and nothing is kept.
branches.cn: 努力线：力气倒进去，什么也没留下。

branches.en: THE OUTCOME: when the result is fixed, more pouring changes nothing.
branches.cn: 结局线：结果已定，再倒也没用。

branches.en: THE SPEECH: words run out of the vessel as fast as they are poured in.
branches.cn: 言语线：话刚倒进去就流走了。

branches.en: THE TREATMENT: medicine pours care into a body that cannot hold it.
branches.cn: 治疗线：医学把照料倒进一个盛不住的身体。

branches.en: Effort and empty talk fail for the same reason: neither leaves anything behind.
branches.cn: 努力与空谈因同一个原因落空：两者都没留下任何东西。

intro.en: Futile is a Latin adjective borrowed whole; English builds futility, futilely, and futileness on it with -ity, -ly, and -ness.
intro.cn: futile 是整体借入的拉丁语形容词；英语用 -ity、-ly 与 -ness 在它上面构成 futility、futilely 与 futileness。

latinIntro.en: Latin futilis supplies both the leaky image and the sense of vain worthlessness, and futilitas adds the abstract noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 futilis 同时提供「漏水」的意象与「徒劳无价值」的含义，futilitas 则给出抽象名词。

items.meaning: leaky, that will not hold water
items.example: The Latin adjective supplies the core image.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词提供核心意象。

items.example: Classical prose uses it of vain effort.
items.exampleCN: 古典散文用它形容徒劳的努力。

items.example: English borrows the adjective whole in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十六世纪把这个形容词整体借入。

items.example: The suffix marks an adjective of tendency, as in futile and fragile.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示倾向的形容词，如 futile 与 fragile。

items.example: The noun suffix -ity names the quality.
items.exampleCN: 名词后缀 -ity 标出这种性质。

items.example: It forms futility from futile.
items.exampleCN: 它把 futile 变成 futility。

items.example: The adverb describes how an action is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述动作进行的方式。

items.example: It forms futilely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 futilely。

items.example: The suffix -ness gives a second noun form.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 给出第二个名词形式。

items.example: It forms futileness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 futileness。

definition_zh: 急促含糊地说；喋喋不休；急促含糊的话；嘎嘎声
definition_en: to speak too fast and unclearly, or such speech; also the repeated noise made by geese
core_image: 鸭子被追时脖子一伸，一串含混的音节连着滚出来
scene: 电话那头很吵，老人越说越快，句子挤在一起，听的人只好反复请他放慢。The old man gabbled into the phone until nobody could follow him.
sceneCN: 这里 gabble 是「急促含糊地说」（第 1 个义项：说得又快又不清楚）；句意：老人对着电话急促含糊地说，最后没人听得懂。

pos.zh: 动词：急促含糊地说；喋喋不休地说
名词：急促含糊的话；嘎嘎声

derivatives.zh: 由 gabble 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「说话急促含糊的人」
由 gabble 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「急促含糊的话；絮叨」

senses.title: To speak fast and unclearly
senses.definition: to speak quickly and indistinctly, so that words run into one another
senses.definitionCN: 说得又快又不清楚，字与字黏连在一起
senses.example: Nervous, he gabbled his excuse and looked at the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他紧张地含糊说出了借口，眼睛盯着地板。
senses.why: The word imitates a stream of sound that comes out faster than it can be shaped into clear words.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿一串声音，出口的速度快过来得及咬清字音。

senses.title: To talk too much about nothing
senses.definition: to talk on and on without saying anything worth hearing
senses.definitionCN: 一直说下去，却没有说出任何值得听的内容
senses.example: She gabbled about the weather for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她絮絮叨叨地讲了十分钟天气。
senses.why: Once the sound is detached from meaning, quantity replaces content: more noise, less said.
senses.whyCN: 声音一旦与意义脱钩，数量就取代了内容：噪声更多，说的却更少。

senses.title: A stream of unclear speech
senses.definition: a rapid, indistinct flow of words or voices that cannot be separated into clear units
senses.definitionCN: 又快又模糊的一串话语或人声，无法切分成清晰的单位
senses.example: From the back room came a gabble of excited voices.
senses.exampleCN: 从后屋传来一阵兴奋而含糊的人声。
senses.why: The verb turns into a noun for the whole lump of sound, not for any single word inside it.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，指整团声音，而不是其中任何一个字。

senses.title: The cry of geese
senses.definition: the noisy, repeated cry of geese or similar birds
senses.definitionCN: 鹅或类似鸟类发出的响亮而重复的叫声
senses.example: A gabble of geese rose from the pond at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮时，池塘上响起一片鹅的嘎嘎声。
senses.why: The same imitative sound names the bird noise that first suggested the human speech sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拟声词也用来指鸟叫，而人对「含糊快语」的感觉正是从这种鸟叫来的。

senses.title: Empty talk as a habit
senses.titleCN: 空话；废话（作不可数名词）
senses.definition: talk that is all sound and no content, treated as a settled habit or a quality of speech
senses.definitionCN: 只有声音而没有内容的谈话，被视为固定的习惯或说话品质
senses.example: The speech was pure gabble, full of names and empty of ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇讲话纯粹是空话，满是名号，却没有思想。
senses.why: The noun extends from one burst of unclear sound to a settled habit of speaking without substance.
senses.whyCN: 名词从「一阵含糊的声音」扩展到「说话没有实质」的固定习惯。

intro.en: Gabble is imitative in origin: it echoes the rush of sound it names, and it is first recorded in English in the sixteenth century alongside the shorter verb gab.
intro.cn: gabble 属于拟声来源：它模仿所命名的急促声音，十六世纪与较短的动词 gab 一起出现在英语中。

items.en: The word is probably echoic, built to sound like a rush of half-formed syllables.
items.cn: 这个词大概是拟声的，读音就像一串没咬清的音节冲出来。

items.en: Gab, a shorter verb meaning to talk or to mock, is already at hand before the longer form appears.
items.cn: 在较长的形式出现之前，表示「说话、嘲弄」的较短动词 gab 已经存在。

items.en: Gabble is recorded in the sixteenth century for rapid, indistinct human speech.
items.cn: gabble 在十六世纪被记录，指又快又不清楚的人声。

items.en: The noun extends to the noise of geese and to crowded, confused voices.
items.cn: 名词扩展到鹅的叫声，以及拥挤混乱的人声。

items.en: Modern dictionaries keep the core sense of fast, unclear speech and label the word informal.
items.cn: 现代词典保留「又快又不清楚」的核心义，并把这个词标为口语体。

note.en: The look-alike group holds gab and its family plus one goose word; the near-meaning group holds verbs for talking too much or too fast.
note.cn: 形近组收 gab 及其词族，另加一个与鹅有关的词；近义组收表示「话太多、太快」的动词。

entries.definition: To talk idly or to chat; the shorter verb behind gabble.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「闲聊、空谈」，是 gabble 背后较短的动词。

entries.definition: Talkative, fond of chatting; an informal word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「爱唠叨的、话多的」，属于口语词。

entries.definition: To eat fast, or the cry of a turkey; only the sound resembles gabble.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「狼吞虎咽」或指火鸡的叫声；只是发音与 gabble 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To speak in a way that is hard to understand, often from excitement or confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「含糊不清地说」，常因激动或慌乱而如此。

entries.definition: To talk quickly and continuously about unimportant things.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「喋喋不休地聊」一些小事。

entries.definition: To talk fast in a way that sounds like noise to the listener.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「叽里咕噜地说」，在听者耳中近乎噪声。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the echoic origin, the gab family, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用拟声来源、gab 词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Gabble sounds like what it means: a run of syllables with no gap for breath.
normal.cn: gabble 的读音就像它的意思：一串没有换气空隙的音节。

normal.en: The short verb gab means to chat, and gabble is the same talk speeded up and blurred.
normal.cn: 较短的动词 gab 表示闲聊，gabble 就是同样的谈话被加速、被糊成一团。

normal.en: Gabble away and gabble on both suggest a speaker who will not stop.
normal.cn: gabble away 与 gabble on 都暗示说话人停不下来。

normal.en: To gabble out a message is to push the words out before they are formed.
normal.cn: gabble out 一句话，就是在字还没成形时就把话推出去。

normal.en: Geese gabble: the bird noise and the human rush of words share one echoic source.
normal.cn: 鹅会 gabble：鸟叫与人话的急促共享同一个拟声来源。

abstract.en: Picture a man on the phone, words falling over each other like coins spilled from a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人打电话，字句互相绊倒，像硬币从口袋里撒出来。

abstract.en: Picture a talkative neighbour at the gate, producing ten minutes of sound and one fact.
abstract.cn: 想象门口健谈的邻居，说了十分钟的声音，只给出一条事实。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded bus where every passenger speaks at once, and no sentence can be picked out.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤的公交车上每个人同时开口，没有一句话能被挑出来。

examples.en: He gabbled an apology and hurried out of the room.
examples.cn: 他急促含糊地道了歉，匆匆走出房间。

examples.en: The children gabbled about the film all the way home.
examples.cn: 孩子们一路叽叽喳喳地聊那部电影。

examples.en: A gabble of voices came through the wall.
examples.cn: 一阵含糊嘈杂的人声从墙那边传来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎布」——像鸭子被追时「嘎布嘎布」叫个不停，话又快又含混；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拟声词，一般认为模仿急促含混的连续音节；十六世纪进入英语，与较早的 gab（闲聊、嘲弄）同族，可能受荷兰语 gabberen（喋喋不休）与德语 gabbern 影响，确切来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses run from the act of speaking fast, through empty talk and a burst of unclear voices, to the cry of geese and the habit of saying nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从「说得又快又含糊」这一动作出发，经空谈、一阵含糊的人声，到鹅的叫声，最后指「说了等于没说」的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream of half-formed syllables tumbling out of a mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串没咬清的音节从嘴里翻滚出来。

branches.en: THE ACT: words come out faster than they can be shaped.
branches.cn: 动作线：话出口的速度快过来得及成形。

branches.en: THE HABIT: sound continues after meaning has stopped.
branches.cn: 习惯线：意义停下之后，声音还在继续。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: the whole lump of unclear speech becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 产物线：整团含糊的话语变成名词。

branches.en: THE BIRD: geese repeat the same blurred sound.
branches.cn: 鸟线：鹅重复着同样的含混声音。

branches.en: Fast speech and empty talk meet when speed replaces content.
branches.cn: 当速度取代内容时，快语与空谈就合流了。

intro.en: Gabble is an echoic English verb; its family is built with gab, -er, -ing, and the noun use of the same form.
intro.cn: gabble 是拟声的英语动词；它的词族由 gab、-er、-ing 以及同一形式的名称用法构成。

latinIntro.en: Gabble has no Latin source; it belongs to an echoic Germanic group, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: gabble 没有拉丁语来源，属于拟声的日耳曼语词群，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The verb is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The shorter verb is the older cousin.
items.exampleCN: 这个较短的动词是更早的近亲。

items.meaningCN: 表反复或持续动作的动词后缀
items.example: The suffix suggests repeated or continued sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀暗示反复或持续的声音。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person.
items.exampleCN: 施事后缀标出这类人。

items.example: It forms gabbler.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gabbler。

items.example: The gerund names the activity and its product.
items.exampleCN: 动名词标出这一活动及其产物。

items.example: It forms gabbling.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gabbling。

items.example: The past tense marks a finished burst of speech.
items.exampleCN: 过去式标出一阵已经结束的快语。

items.example: The same form also works as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一形式也作名词使用。

definition_zh: 小装置；小器具；小巧的电子设备；花哨的小玩意儿
definition_en: a small, cleverly made object or device, often a new or electronic one and sometimes regarded as unnecessary
core_image: 桌上摊着一只巴掌大的小盒子，按钮亮着，用途却一时说不清
scene: 礼物拆开后，桌上多了一个巴掌大的小东西，翻来覆去看不出该怎么用。The little gadget had three buttons and no instructions.
sceneCN: 这里 gadget 是「小装置、小器具」（第 1 个义项：小巧而精巧的器具）；句意：这个小装置有三个按钮，却没有说明书。

pos.zh: 名词：小装置；小器具；小巧的电子设备；花哨的小玩意儿

derivatives.zh: 由 gadget 加集合名词后缀 -ry 构成，义为「小装置的总称」
由 gadget 加表人后缀 -eer 构成，义为「热衷发明或摆弄小装置的人」

senses.title: A small clever device
senses.definition: a small object or tool, usually cleverly designed and often new
senses.definitionCN: 小巧的物件或工具，通常设计得巧妙，而且往往是新出的
senses.example: He opened the box and found a gadget for slicing apples.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开盒子，发现一个切苹果用的小器具。
senses.why: The word names a small made thing whose value lies in a clever mechanism rather than in size.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指一件被做出来的小东西，价值在巧妙的机关而不在体积。

senses.title: An electronic consumer device
senses.definition: a compact electronic device, especially a new one bought for convenience or pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 紧凑的电子设备，尤指为了便利或消遣而新买的
senses.example: Her bag was full of gadgets: a tiny camera, a tracker, and two chargers.
senses.exampleCN: 她包里塞满小设备：一台微型相机、一个追踪器，还有两个充电器。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the clever small thing becomes electric, and the word follows the market.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪，精巧的小东西带上电，词义便随市场一起转向电子消费设备。

senses.title: A small attachment or accessory
senses.definition: a small extra piece fitted to a larger tool or machine to do a special job
senses.definitionCN: 装到较大的工具或机器上、用来做某项特殊工作的小附加件
senses.example: The drill came with a gadget that holds screws steady.
senses.exampleCN: 这把电钻配了一个能把螺丝固定住的小配件。
senses.why: From a separate object to an added part: the gadget is the clever piece attached to something bigger.
senses.whyCN: 从独立物件变成附加部件：gadget 成了装在大东西上的巧妙零件。

senses.title: A pointless or showy trifle
senses.definition: an object that seems clever but has little real use, often bought on impulse
senses.definitionCN: 看上去巧妙却没有多少实际用途的物件，常是冲动购买
senses.example: The kitchen drawer is full of gadgets nobody ever uses.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房抽屉里塞满了没人用过的小玩意儿。
senses.why: Once cleverness is admired for itself, the same word can mock an object that solves a problem nobody has.
senses.whyCN: 当「巧妙」本身被欣赏时，同一个词也能讥讽那些解决不存在的问题的物件。

senses.title: A small software tool
senses.definition: a small program or feature that performs one limited task, often added to a larger system
senses.definitionCN: 只完成一项有限任务的小程序或功能，常被加进更大的系统里
senses.example: The site offers a gadget that converts file sizes in one click.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站提供一个小工具，点一下就能转换文件大小单位。
senses.why: Software borrows the physical image: a compact tool that does one job and sits inside a bigger machine.
senses.whyCN: 软件借用了实物意象：一件只做一件事、装在更大机器里的小工具。

intro.en: Gadget appeared in English in the nineteenth century, and its origin is uncertain; the most cited guess links it to a French word for a small catch in a mechanism.
intro.cn: gadget 于十九世纪出现在英语中，来源不确定；被引用最多的猜测把它与法语中表示机械小卡扣的词联系起来。

items.en: No source is proved; the word is first recorded in the nineteenth century in nautical and mechanical contexts.
items.cn: 没有任何来源得到证实；这个词最早见于十九世纪的航海与机械语境。

items.en: Gachette, a small catch or pawl in a lock or a gun, is one commonly suggested source.
items.cn: gachette 指锁具或枪械上的小卡扣，是常被提到的来源之一。

items.en: Gadget is recorded in print in the 1880s for a small mechanical aid.
items.cn: gadget 在十九世纪八十年代的印刷品中出现，指机械小辅助件。

items.en: Mass-produced household and electric gadgets make the word an everyday label for clever consumer objects.
items.cn: 批量生产的家用与电器小装置，使这个词成为精巧消费品的日常称呼。

items.en: Gadget extends to software widgets and to gadgetry as a collective name.
items.cn: gadget 扩展到软件小工具，并以 gadgetry 作为总称。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on gadget and one sound-alike; the near-meaning group holds other names for small devices.
note.cn: 形近组收由 gadget 构成的词与一个发音相近的词；近义组收其他表示「小设备」的词。

entries.definition: Small devices as a group, often used with a slight tone of criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小装置的总称」，常带轻微贬义，由 gadget 加 -ry 构成。

entries.definition: A person who loves inventing or collecting gadgets.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「热衷发明或收集小装置的人」，由 gadget 加 -eer 构成。

entries.definition: A small device or, in software, a small interface tool; only the sound resembles gadget.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小装置」，在软件中指小界面工具；只是发音与 gadget 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A piece of equipment made for a particular purpose, broader and more neutral than gadget.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装置、设备」，比 gadget 更宽泛、更中性。

entries.definition: A machine for household use, such as a fridge or a washing machine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「家用电器」，如冰箱或洗衣机。

entries.definition: A strange or badly made machine or device, often described with humour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奇特的装置」，常带调侃意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the uncertain French origin, the -ry and -eer family, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用不确定的法语来源、带 -ry 与 -eer 的词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Gadget is a small thing with a clever inside: the smaller it is, the more the cleverness shows.
normal.cn: gadget 是外表小巧、内里巧妙的东西：越小，巧劲越显眼。

normal.en: Gadgetry is the collective noun, and it usually carries a raised eyebrow.
normal.cn: gadgetry 是集合名词，通常带着一点不以为然的语气。

normal.en: A gadgeteer is the person who buys, builds, and cannot throw away these things.
normal.cn: gadgeteer 就是那种买、做、又舍不得扔掉这些小东西的人。

normal.en: Kitchen gadget and electronic gadget name the two places the word lives.
normal.cn: kitchen gadget 与 electronic gadget 标出这个词最常出现的两个场景。

normal.en: A useless gadget solves a problem that nobody had.
normal.cn: useless gadget 解决的是一个根本不存在的问题。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer of small chrome tools, each with one button and one purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉亮闪闪的小工具，每个只有一个按钮、一种用途。

abstract.en: Picture a phone that can do a hundred things, and a person using it to check the time.
abstract.cn: 想象一部能做上百件事的手机，而人只用它看时间。

abstract.en: Picture a corkscrew with three hinges and a lamp, opening one bottle slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带三处铰链和一盏灯的开瓶器，慢慢开一只瓶子。

examples.en: The kitchen drawer is full of gadgets that seemed useful in the shop.
examples.cn: 厨房抽屉里塞满了在店里看着有用的小玩意儿。

examples.en: This gadget tracks your sleep without a phone.
examples.cn: 这个小设备不用手机就能记录睡眠。

examples.en: Engineers laughed at the contraption, but the gadget worked.
examples.cn: 工程师们笑那个怪装置，可这个小东西还真管用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎吉特」——按一下「嘎」一声的小机器，就是小装置；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定，十九世纪进入英语，最初指机械或航海上的小辅助件；最常被引用的猜测是法语 gachette（锁具或枪械上的小卡扣），但没有定论；二十世纪随家电与电子产品普及而定型为「精巧小装置」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from a clever small object to its electric form, an added attachment, a showy trifle, and a small software tool.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从精巧的小物件，走到电子形态、附加配件、花哨无用之物，最后是软件小工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm-sized box with three buttons and no instructions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只巴掌大的盒子，三个按钮，没有说明书。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: small size, clever mechanism.
branches.cn: 物件线：体积小，机关巧。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: electricity turns the clever box into a consumer device.
branches.cn: 电流线：电把巧妙的小盒变成消费设备。

branches.en: THE ATTACHMENT: the clever piece is fitted onto a larger tool.
branches.cn: 配件线：巧妙的小件被装到更大的工具上。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: cleverness without use becomes a trifle.
branches.cn: 评判线：没有用途的巧妙沦为小玩意儿。

branches.en: Hardware and software both hold a small tool that does one job.
branches.cn: 硬件与软件都容得下只做一件事的小工具。

intro.en: Gadget is an English coinage of uncertain origin; English builds gadgetry and gadgeteer on it with -ry and -eer.
intro.cn: gadget 是来源不确定的英语新造词；英语用 -ry 与 -eer 在它上面构成 gadgetry 与 gadgeteer。

latinIntro.en: Gadget has no Latin source: the suggested trail leads to French, and no Latin kin can be listed.
latinIntro.cn: gadget 没有拉丁语来源：可循的线索指向法语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The base noun names the object.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词指这件东西。

items.example: The suffix -ry makes a collective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ry 构成集合名词。

items.example: It forms gadgetry.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gadgetry。

items.example: The suffix -eer names a person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -eer 标出一类人。

items.example: It forms gadgeteer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gadgeteer。

items.example: The plural adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数加 -s。

items.example: It forms gadgets.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gadgets。

items.meaning: a small catch in a mechanism
items.example: The French word is one suggested source.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语词是猜测的来源之一。

items.example: The compound adjective describes a look.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形容词描述外观。

definition_zh: 反驳；否认；与……相抵触；反对
definition_en: to deny or contradict a statement, or to oppose something, used mainly in formal and literary English
core_image: 有人把一张纸摊在桌上，另一个人伸手把它推了回去
scene: 会上有人提出一个说法，坐在对面的人立刻摇头，把那份记录推了回去。No one dared gainsay the old engineer when he questioned the figures.
sceneCN: 这里 gainsay 是「反驳、否认」（第 1 个义项：当面否定别人说的话）；句意：老工程师质疑那些数字时，没人敢反驳他。

pos.zh: 动词：反驳；否认；与……相抵触；反对（多用于正式或书面语）

derivatives.zh: 由 gainsay 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「反驳者；否认者」
由 gainsay 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「反驳；否认」

senses.title: To contradict someone to their face
senses.definition: to speak against what someone has just said, especially in public or formal settings
senses.definitionCN: 对某人刚说的话说反话，尤指在公开或正式场合
senses.example: Several delegates tried to gainsay the chairman, but the vote went ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 几位代表试图反驳主席，但表决还是照常进行。
senses.why: The prefix gain- means against, so gainsay is literally to say against: speech set opposite speech.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 gain- 意为「反对」，所以 gainsay 字面就是「对着说」：用话去顶话。

senses.title: To deny a statement or fact
senses.definition: to deny that a statement or fact is true
senses.definitionCN: 否认某个说法或事实为真
senses.example: The report gainsaid the official account of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告否定了官方对事故的说法。
senses.why: Saying against a claim can also mean refusing it as false, not merely arguing with it.
senses.whyCN: 对着一个说法说话，也可以是不承认它为真，而不只是与它争辩。

senses.title: To be contradicted by evidence
senses.definition: of evidence, facts, or results: to show that a claim is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 指证据、事实或结果：表明某个说法是错的
senses.example: The new measurements gainsay the earlier estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 新的测量结果否定了早先的估算。
senses.why: The action reverses direction: evidence now does the saying against, and the claim is the thing denied.
senses.whyCN: 动作方向反了过来：由证据来「对着说」，被否认的成了那个说法。

senses.title: To oppose a plan or an action
senses.definition: to oppose or resist a plan, proposal, or course of action
senses.definitionCN: 反对或抵制某项计划、提议或行动方案
senses.example: The council would not gainsay a plan that had local support.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不愿反对一个得到当地支持的计划。
senses.why: Opposition widens from words to action: to gainsay a plan is to stand against it before it starts.
senses.whyCN: 反对从言语扩展到行动：gainsay 一个计划，就是在它开始之前站到它的对立面。

senses.title: To refuse, in older usage
senses.definition: to refuse or decline something, an older sense now rare outside historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝或谢绝某物，这一旧义如今只见于历史题材的文字
senses.example: In the old tale the knight gainsays the gift and rides on.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的故事里，骑士拒绝了礼物，继续策马前行。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word includes refusal, since to say against an offer is to turn it down.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层还包含「拒绝」：对着一个提议说反话，就是把它推掉。

intro.en: Gainsay is a native English compound of gain, meaning against, and say; the prefix survives from Old English gegn and shares its origin with again.
intro.cn: gainsay 是英语本土的复合词，由表示「反对」的 gain 与 say 组成；这个前缀来自古英语 gegn，与 again 同出一源。

items.en: Gegn means against or opposite, and it survives in English as the rare prefix gain-.
items.cn: 古英语 gegn 意为「反对、相对」，在英语中作为罕见前缀 gain- 留存下来。

items.en: Gainsayen combines gain, against, with sayen, to say: to speak against.
items.cn: 中古英语 gainsayen 把表示「反对」的 gain 与 sayen（说）组合起来，义为「对着说」。

items.en: The verb is common in ordinary speech and in law, where a party may gainsay a claim.
items.cn: 这个动词在普通言语与法律中都很常见，当事人可以 gainsay 一项主张。

items.en: Everyday use fades, and gainsay becomes a formal and literary word, often in the passive.
items.cn: 日常用法渐渐消失，gainsay 变成正式而书面化的词，常用于被动式。

items.en: Today the verb survives mainly in the fixed phrase cannot be gainsaid.
items.cn: 今天这个词主要活在固定说法 cannot be gainsaid 中。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the gain- family and a false friend; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of denial and contradiction.
note.cn: 形近组收 gain- 词族与一个形近假朋友；近义组收其他表示「否认、反驳」的动词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of gainsay, formed with the older past of say.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，gainsay 的过去式与过去分词，由 say 的旧式过去分词构成。

entries.definition: A person who contradicts or denies, formed with the agent suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反驳者、否认者」，由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: To obtain or increase; a separate word from a different source, close to gainsay only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得、增加」；与 gainsay 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To state the opposite of what someone has said; the everyday equivalent of gainsay.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「反驳、与……矛盾」，是 gainsay 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: To say that something is not true, or to refuse to admit it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「否认、拒不承认」。

entries.definition: To argue against a statement or claim, often in public or legal settings.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「对……提出异议、争辩」，多用于公开或法律场合。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real gain- prefix, the fixed passive phrase, and the small family around gainsay.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的 gain- 前缀、固定的被动说法，以及 gainsay 周围的小词族。

normal.en: Gain here does not mean obtain: the prefix means against, so gainsay is to say against.
normal.cn: 这里的 gain 不是「获得」：这个前缀意为「反对」，所以 gainsay 就是「对着说」。

normal.en: Cannot be gainsaid is the phrase that keeps the verb alive: it means impossible to deny.
normal.cn: cannot be gainsaid 是让这个动词活下来的说法：意思是「无可否认」。

normal.en: A gainsayer is simply a person who says against you.
normal.cn: gainsayer 就是「对着你说」的人，即反驳者。

normal.en: The verb is formal: in speech most people say contradict or deny instead.
normal.cn: 这个词很正式：口语里多数人会用 contradict 或 deny。

normal.en: Gainsaid is both the past tense and the past participle, so one form does two jobs.
normal.cn: gainsaid 既是过去式也是过去分词，一个形式兼两职。

abstract.en: Picture two people holding the same sheet of paper and pulling it in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人拿着同一张纸，朝相反方向拉。

abstract.en: Picture a claim written on a card, and a hand turning the card face down.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片上写着一个说法，一只手把卡片翻过去扣下。

abstract.en: Picture a row of old measurements crossed out by a fresh line of figures.
abstract.cn: 想象一排旧数据被一行新的数字划掉。

examples.en: Few historians would gainsay the importance of that year.
examples.cn: 很少有历史学家会否认那一年的重要性。

examples.en: His honesty cannot be gainsaid.
examples.cn: 他的诚实无可否认。

examples.en: The board did not gainsay the plan, but it asked for more figures.
examples.cn: 董事会没有反对这个计划，但要求提供更多数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给恩说」——别人说一句，你偏要「给」回去一句反话，就是反驳；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 本土复合词：gain-（古英语 gegn，反对、相对）+ say（说）→ 中古英语 gainsayen「对着说」→ 现代英语 gainsay。前缀 gain- 与 again 同出一源，义为「反对、相反」；现代主要留在 cannot be gainsaid 等正式说法中。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one movement of speech against speech: contradicting a person, denying a claim, being contradicted by evidence, opposing a plan, and refusing an offer in older use.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿着「用话顶话」这一个动作展开：当面反驳、否认说法、被证据否定、反对计划，以及古义中的拒绝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of paper pushed back across a table by a flat hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一张纸从桌面上推回去。

branches.en: THE PERSON: one speaker answers another with a counter word.
branches.cn: 人物线：一个说话人用反话回应另一个。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: the statement itself is refused as false.
branches.cn: 说法线：被拒绝的是说法本身的真实性。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: the saying against is done by facts, not by people.
branches.cn: 证据线：「对着说」的动作由事实完成，而不是人。

branches.en: THE PLAN: opposition moves from words to a course of action.
branches.cn: 计划线：反对从言语转到行动方案。

branches.en: Denying a claim and refusing an offer are both ways of saying no.
branches.cn: 否认一个说法与拒绝一个提议，都是说「不」的方式。

intro.en: Gainsay is a native compound, so its word formation is Germanic: the prefix gain- plus say, with -er and -ing added in English.
intro.cn: gainsay 是本土复合词，构词属于日耳曼语式：前缀 gain- 加 say，再由英语加上 -er 与 -ing。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source: the word is built from Old English materials, and its Latin-looking synonym contradict belongs to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源：它由古英语材料构成，看似拉丁语的近义词 contradict 属于另一个词族。

items.example: The prefix carries the whole idea of opposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀承载了「反对」的全部意思。

items.example: It supplies the act of speaking.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「说」这个动作。

items.example: The compound is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式就是基础动词。

items.example: The old past form of say survives here.
items.exampleCN: say 的旧式过去形式在这里留存。

items.example: It marks the finished action.
items.exampleCN: 它标出已完成的动作。

items.meaning: the act of denying or opposing
items.example: The gerund names the act.
items.exampleCN: 动名词指这一行为。

items.example: It forms gainsaying.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gainsaying。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person.
items.exampleCN: 施事后缀标出这类人。

items.example: It forms gainsayer.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gainsayer。

definition_zh: 大风；狂风；暴风雨；（笑声等的）一阵爆发
definition_en: a very strong wind, a storm, or a sudden noisy outburst of laughter
core_image: 海边的草全部压向一侧，浪头被风撕成白沫
scene: 渔船回港时，桅杆被吹得嗡嗡作响，岸上的人抓紧缆绳。A sudden gale tore the sails before the crew could reef them.
sceneCN: 这里 gale 是「大风、狂风」（第 1 个义项：风力极强的风）；句意：船员还来不及收帆，一阵狂风就把帆撕破了。

pos.zh: 名词：大风；狂风；暴风雨；笑声、掌声等的一阵爆发

derivatives.zh: 由 gale 与 force 复合而成，义为「风力七级以上的、猛烈的」
由 gale 与 warning 复合而成，义为「大风警报」

senses.title: A very strong wind
senses.definition: a wind of great strength, especially one strong enough to trouble ships and buildings
senses.definitionCN: 力量极大的风，尤指强到能威胁船只与建筑的风
senses.example: A gale stripped the scaffolding from the unfinished tower.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵狂风把未完工的塔楼上的脚手架掀掉了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply moving air at high speed, the force that bends grass and tears canvas.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是高速流动的空气，那股把草压弯、把帆布撕开的力量。

senses.title: A storm at sea
senses.definition: a storm with very strong winds, especially at sea
senses.definitionCN: 伴随极强风的暴风雨，尤指发生在海上
senses.example: The fleet waited in harbour until the gale had passed.
senses.exampleCN: 船队在港里等待，直到风暴过去。
senses.why: At sea a strong wind is not weather but danger, so the word grows into the whole storm.
senses.whyCN: 在海上，强风不只是天气而是危险，于是这个词长成了整场风暴。

senses.title: A stated wind force
senses.definition: a wind of force seven to ten on the Beaufort scale, as used in shipping forecasts
senses.definitionCN: 蒲福风级上七到十级的风，用于航运预报
senses.example: Shipping forecasts warned of a gale in the western approaches.
senses.exampleCN: 航运预报警告西部近海水域将有大风。
senses.why: Sailors needed numbers, so the old word for strong wind became a rung on a measured scale.
senses.whyCN: 水手需要数字，于是表示强风的旧词成了测量刻度上的一档。

senses.title: A burst of laughter or sound
senses.definition: a sudden loud outburst of laughter, applause, or similar sound
senses.definitionCN: 突然爆发的一阵响亮笑声、掌声或类似声音
senses.example: The joke set off a gale of laughter in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那个笑话在礼堂里引起一阵哄堂大笑。
senses.why: The storm image moves to sound: laughter that arrives with force and sweeps the room like wind.
senses.whyCN: 风暴意象转到声音：笑声带着力道袭来，像风一样扫过整个房间。

senses.title: A gentle breeze, in older poetry
senses.definition: a light breeze, a poetic sense found in older verse and now rare
senses.definitionCN: 轻柔的风，见于较早诗歌，如今罕见
senses.example: In the old song a gale stirs the curtains and the sleeper smiles.
senses.exampleCN: 在那首古老的歌里，一阵轻风拂动窗帘，睡着的人露出微笑。
senses.why: Before the modern sense hardened, the word could name any moving air, including the soft wind of a summer evening.
senses.whyCN: 在现代义固定之前，这个词可以指任何流动的空气，包括夏夜那种轻柔的风。

intro.en: Gale is recorded in Middle English for a strong wind; its deeper origin is uncertain, with rival suggestions from Old Norse and from a Germanic root meaning to shout.
intro.cn: gale 在中古英语中已指强风；更早的来源不确定，有来自古诺尔斯语与日耳曼语「喊叫」词根两种说法。

items.en: No single source is proved; the word appears in Middle English and its earlier history is disputed.
items.cn: 没有单一来源得到证实；这个词见于中古英语，更早的历史有争议。

items.en: A hypothetical gal, a gust or screaming wind, is one suggested source, but the form is reconstructed.
items.cn: 假设的古诺尔斯语 gal（一阵狂风）是猜测的来源之一，但该形式是重构的。

items.en: Others connect it with a Germanic root meaning to shout or sing, the same root that yields English yell.
items.cn: 另一些看法把它与日耳曼语中表示「喊叫、歌唱」的词根联系，也就是英语 yell 的来源。

items.en: Nautical use fixes gale as a named wind force in sailing records.
items.cn: 航海用法把 gale 固定为航行记录中有名字的风力等级。

items.en: The word extends to outbursts of laughter and to fixed compounds such as gale-force.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到笑声的爆发，以及 gale-force 这类固定复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds compounds and one false friend; the near-meaning group holds other words for strong wind and storm.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个形近假朋友；近义组收其他表示「强风、风暴」的词。

entries.definition: Of a wind: of the strength that warrants a gale warning, used before nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「七级以上的、猛烈的」，用于名词前，由 gale 与 force 复合而成。

entries.definition: An official notice that a gale is expected, issued for shipping and coasts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大风警报」，为航运与沿海发布的正式通知。

entries.definition: To entertain someone with stories or food; it comes from a French root and only sounds like gale.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「以故事或食物款待」；词源来自法语，只是发音与 gale 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Moving air in general, from a breath to a storm; the neutral word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风」，从一口气到风暴都可用，是最中性的词。

entries.definition: A brief, sudden rush of wind, shorter than a gale.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一阵突发的风」，比 gale 短促。

entries.definition: A violent storm, a literary and formal word stronger than gale.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暴风雨」，书面而正式，比 gale 更强。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the storm image, the nautical scale, the laughter sense, and the compounds built around gale.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用风暴意象、航海风力等级、笑声义项，以及 gale 周围的复合词。

normal.en: A gale is wind with a job to do: it bends trees, tears canvas, and closes ports.
normal.cn: gale 是有「任务」的风：压弯树、撕破帆、让港口关闭。

normal.en: Gale-force is the adjective for winds strong enough to trigger a gale warning.
normal.cn: gale-force 是形容风力强到触发大风警报的形容词。

normal.en: The Beaufort scale gives gale a number, so sailors can speak of force eight without adjectives.
normal.cn: 蒲福风级给 gale 一个数字，水手不说形容词也能说「八级」。

normal.en: A gale of laughter borrows the storm: it arrives fast, loud, and impossible to stop.
normal.cn: a gale of laughter 借用了风暴：来得快、响，而且停不下来。

normal.en: Words like galore and regale only look related; gale has no English family of its own.
normal.cn: galore 与 regale 这类词只是看起来相关，gale 并没有自己的英语词族。

abstract.en: Picture grass on a headland all bent one way, as if combed by a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象海岬上的草全被压向一边，像被一只手梳过。

abstract.en: Picture a harbour full of boats waiting, masts stripped and hatches battened.
abstract.cn: 想象港口里挤满等风的船，桅杆空了，舱口钉死。

abstract.en: Picture a shipping forecast read aloud, one number carrying a whole night of danger.
abstract.cn: 想象广播里念出航运预报，一个数字就装着一整夜的危险。

examples.en: A gale blew all night and took the roof off the shed.
examples.cn: 狂风刮了一整夜，把小棚的屋顶掀掉了。

examples.en: The forecast warned of gales along the northern coast.
examples.cn: 预报警告北部沿海将有大风。

examples.en: Her remark set off a gale of laughter at the table.
examples.cn: 她的一句话在桌边引起一阵哄笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盖了」——风大得像要把屋顶都「盖」过去，就是狂风；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 gale（强风）→ 现代英语 gale。更早来源不确定：一说来自古诺尔斯语重构形式 gal（一阵狂风），一说与日耳曼语中表示「喊叫、歌唱」的词根有关（英语 yell 同源），两说并存；十六世纪起航海用语把它固定为有名称的风力等级，现代又扩展出「一阵笑声」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow the force of air: a strong wind, a sea storm, a numbered wind force, a burst of laughter, and a rare poetic breeze.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿着风力展开：强风、海上风暴、编号的风力等级、一阵笑声，以及罕见的诗歌「轻风」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: coastal grass flattened to one side while white spray leaves the wave tops.
core.cn: 核心意象：海岸的草全被压向一侧，浪尖被撕成白沫。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: air moving with enough force to bend and tear.
branches.cn: 天气线：空气以足以压弯、撕开物体的力量流动。

branches.en: THE SEA: the same wind becomes a storm that keeps ships in port.
branches.cn: 海洋线：同一阵风变成把船困在港里的风暴。

branches.en: THE SCALE: sailors give the wind a number and a warning.
branches.cn: 刻度线：水手给风一个数字与一份警报。

branches.en: THE SOUND: laughter arrives with the same force and sweep.
branches.cn: 声音线：笑声以同样的力量与扫荡感袭来。

branches.en: THE OLD POETRY: before the modern sense, any moving air could be a gale.
branches.cn: 古诗线：在现代义固定之前，任何流动的空气都可以叫 gale。

intro.en: Gale is a bare noun with no living suffixes; English builds compounds such as gale-force and gale warning around it.
intro.cn: gale 是没有任何现存后缀的单纯名词；英语围绕它构成 gale-force 与 gale warning 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Gale has no Latin source; the suggested trails are North Germanic, and no Latin kin is listed.
latinIntro.cn: gale 没有拉丁语来源：可循的线索属于北日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The bare noun is the base of the compounds.
items.exampleCN: 这个单纯名词是各复合词的基础。

items.example: The plural adds -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数加 -s。

items.example: It forms gales.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 gales。

items.meaning: of the strength of a gale
items.example: Force joins the noun to describe wind strength.
items.exampleCN: force 与名词组合，用来描述风力。

items.example: It supplies the measuring idea in the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它在这个复合词里提供「强度」的概念。

items.example: Warning turns the noun into an official message.
items.exampleCN: warning 把这个名词变成一份官方通告。

items.example: It supplies the official part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它提供复合词中的官方通告部分。

items.example: The look-alike verb has a French root, not a Germanic one.
items.exampleCN: 这个形近动词来自法语词根，而非日耳曼语。

definition_zh: （马）疾驰；飞跑；骑马疾驰；疾驰的步态；飞速发展
definition_en: to run fast, especially of a horse, with all four feet off the ground between strides
core_image: 四只马蹄同时离地，鬃毛在风里向后飘
scene: 赛马场上，骑手在最后一段催马加速，马蹄几乎不落地。On the final stretch, the rider urged his horse into a gallop.
sceneCN: 这里 gallop 是「疾驰」（第 1 个义项：马匹四蹄腾空的步态）；句意：在最后一段，骑手催马疾驰。

derivatives.zh: 疾驰者；跑得快的马
飞快的；急剧发展的（如物价飞涨）

senses.title: The fastest gait of a horse
senses.definition: the fastest pace of a horse, in which all four feet leave the ground between strides
senses.definitionCN: 马最快的步态，每一步之间四蹄同时离地
senses.example: The grey mare moved into a gallop along the track.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹灰母马在跑道上加速疾驰起来。
senses.why: The Frankish source meant to run well, and the gait is named for the flying leap of the horse.
senses.whyCN: 法兰克语词源意为「跑得好」，这种步态正是以马腾空飞跃的样子得名。

senses.title: To run at a gallop
senses.definition: of a horse, to run at the fastest gait
senses.definitionCN: 指马以最快的步态奔跑
senses.example: The horses galloped down the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 马群沿着山谷疾驰而下。
senses.why: The verb turns the name of the gait into the action that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把步态的名称转化为产生这种步态的动作。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: of a person or vehicle, to move at great speed
senses.definitionCN: 指人或车辆以极快的速度移动
senses.example: He galloped up the stairs to catch the call.
senses.exampleCN: 他飞奔上楼去接电话。
senses.why: People borrow the horse image whenever speed matters more than grace.
senses.whyCN: 只要强调速度而不在乎姿态，人们就会借用马奔跑的意象。

senses.title: To ride a horse at a gallop
senses.definition: to ride a horse at its fastest gait
senses.definitionCN: 骑着马以最快的步态奔跑
senses.example: She galloped the pony across the meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 她骑着矮种马疾驰穿过草地。
senses.why: The transitive use adds a rider to the picture without changing the core image.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法只是在这幅画里加上骑手，核心意象并没有改变。

senses.title: A rapid pace of events
senses.definition: a very fast rate of movement or development, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻事态以极快的速度推进或发展
senses.example: The plot moves at a gallop in the final chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 情节在最后一章飞速推进。
senses.why: Once the horse image is released from the track, any fast process can gallop.
senses.whyCN: 一旦马的意象离开赛道，任何快速推进的过程都可以「疾驰」。

intro.en: Gallop reached English through Old French, but the root is Germanic: the Franks described a horse that ran well.
intro.cn: gallop 经古法语进入英语，但词根属于日耳曼语；一般认为来自法兰克语中「跑得好」的说法。

items.en: The reconstructed form walahlaupan joins that adverb wala, well, and hlaupan, to leap or run.
items.cn: 重构形式 walahlaupan 由副词 wala（好）与 hlaupan（跳、跑）组成。

items.en: Galoper names the horse gait, and the noun galop names the pace itself.
items.cn: galoper 指马疾驰，名词 galop 指这种步态本身。

items.en: Galopen appears in English texts of the fourteenth century.
items.cn: galopen 出现在十四世纪的英语文本中。

items.en: Gallop becomes the standard word for the gait, the ride, and the action.
items.cn: gallop 成为步态、骑乘与动作的标准说法。

items.en: Financial writing extends the word to galloping inflation and galloping growth.
items.cn: 财经写作把该词扩展到恶性通胀与飞速增长。

note.en: Gallop belongs to the horse-gait words and to the Germanic leap family; it has few look-alikes but many near meanings.
note.cn: gallop 属于马匹步态词，也属于日耳曼语「跳」的词族；形近词不多，近义词却不少。

entries.definition: to jump through the air
entries.definitionCN: 跳跃；跃过；与 gallop 同出日耳曼语「跳」的词根

entries.definition: to run with long easy strides
entries.definitionCN: 大步慢跑；与 gallop 共享日耳曼语「跑」的词根

entries.definition: a lively nineteenth-century dance and its music
entries.definitionCN: 十九世纪一种轻快的双人舞及其舞曲，与 gallop 同源借自法语

entries.definition: a moderate two-beat gait of a horse
entries.definitionCN: （马的）小跑；快步，比疾驰慢

entries.definition: a three-beat gait faster than a trot but slower than a gallop
entries.definitionCN: （马的）慢跑步态，比小跑快、比疾驰慢

entries.definition: to run at top speed for a short distance
entries.definitionCN: 短距离全速冲刺

normalIntro.en: Gallop is a horse word with a Germanic leap inside it, and English uses it for any fast rush.
normalIntro.cn: gallop 是个马匹词，内部藏着日耳曼语的「跳」，英语用它形容任何飞速的冲刺。

normal.en: The old Germanic root hlaupan, to leap, also hides in leap.
normal.cn: 古老日耳曼词根 hlaupan（跳）也藏在 leap 里。

normal.en: A horse at a gallop has all four feet off the ground at once.
normal.cn: 马疾驰时四蹄会同时离地。

normal.en: Riders say at a gallop, never in a gallop.
normal.cn: 骑手说 at a gallop，不说 in a gallop。

normal.en: Galloping inflation is a fixed phrase for prices rising out of control.
normal.cn: galloping inflation 是物价失控上涨的固定说法。

normal.en: Compare trot and canter: gallop is the fastest of the three.
normal.cn: 对比 trot 与 canter：gallop 是三种步态里最快的。

abstract.en: See the four hooves hanging in the air for a split second.
abstract.cn: 想象四只马蹄在空中悬停的一瞬。

abstract.en: Hear the drum of hooves that sounds like a heartbeat run wild.
abstract.cn: 听见马蹄声像失控的心跳。

abstract.en: Picture a cyclist flying downhill with the same reckless rush.
abstract.cn: 想象骑车人顺着下坡飞冲而下的那股狠劲。

examples.en: The horse galloped across the open field.
examples.cn: 那匹马疾驰穿过开阔的田野。

examples.en: She rode at a gallop along the wet beach.
examples.cn: 她沿着潮湿的海滩骑马疾驰。

examples.en: Prices were rising at a galloping pace.
examples.cn: 物价正以飞快的速度上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎啦跑」——马蹄踏地嘎啦作响，一溜烟就跑远了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 法兰克语 wala（好）+ hlaupan（跳、跑）→ 古法语 galoper（马疾驰）→ 中古英语 galopen → 英语 gallop，核心义「四蹄腾空地飞跑」。

sensesIntro.en: Gallop starts as the name of the fastest horse pace, passes to the verb for horse, rider, and vehicle, and ends as a figure for rapid growth.
sensesIntro.cn: gallop 先是马最快步态的名称，再转为马、骑手与车辆的动词，最后成为快速发展的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four hooves off the ground at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：四只马蹄在同一瞬间离地。

branches.en: The named gait is the literal centre of the word.
branches.cn: 命名的步态是这个词的字面核心。

branches.en: Horse and rider both gallop, one with legs and one with reins.
branches.cn: 马与骑手都在疾驰，一个靠四蹄，一个靠缰绳。

branches.en: People and vehicles borrow the horse image for pure speed.
branches.cn: 人与车辆借马的意象表达纯粹的速度。

branches.en: The figurative branch lets events and prices gallop as well.
branches.cn: 比喻分支让事态与物价也可以「疾驰」。

branches.en: Both the race track and the market can be described as a gallop.
branches.cn: 赛道与市场都可以用 gallop 来形容。

intro.en: Gallop is a Germanic word dressed in French clothing: the Frankish verb for running well became Old French galoper.
intro.cn: gallop 是穿着法语外衣的日耳曼词：法兰克语中「跑得好」的动词变成了古法语 galoper。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the word comes from Frankish and Old French, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，来自法兰克语与古法语，因此拉丁同源词表为空。

items.example: The first element of the Frankish compound means well.
items.exampleCN: 法兰克语复合词的第一部分意为「好」。

items.example: Hlaupan is the leap inside the horse gait.
items.exampleCN: hlaupan 是马步态里那个「跳」的动作。

items.example: The compound is the reconstructed ancestor of galoper.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 galoper 的重构祖先。

items.example: Old French galoper names the horse gait.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 galoper 指马的疾驰步态。

items.example: The noun galop names the pace itself.
items.exampleCN: 名词 galop 指这种步态本身。

items.example: Middle English texts use galopen for riding fast.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语文本用 galopen 表示骑马快跑。

items.example: The suffix -er forms galloper from gallop.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 从 gallop 构成 galloper。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或持续状态的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms galloping.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 galloping。

items.example: Leap shares the Germanic root hlaupan.
items.exampleCN: leap 共享日耳曼词根 hlaupan。

definition_zh: 匪徒；歹徒；黑帮成员；黑帮题材的
definition_en: a member of a criminal group that uses violence and intimidation
core_image: 夜里收保护费的黑衣人，身后跟着一伙同伙
scene: 码头边的仓库区，夜里总有人来收保护费，商户不敢报警。The gangster demanded a share of every sale in the market.
sceneCN: 这里 gangster 是「黑帮成员」（第 1 个义项：犯罪团伙的成员）；句意：那名黑帮成员要求从市场里的每一笔交易中抽成。

pos.zh: 黑帮题材的；匪徒的（作定语）

derivatives.zh: 黑帮作风；团伙犯罪的行事方式
黑帮地盘；由 gang 与 land 复合而成

senses.title: A member of a criminal gang
senses.definition: a person who belongs to an organized group that commits crimes
senses.definitionCN: 属于有组织犯罪团伙的人
senses.example: The gangster ran a protection racket on the waterfront.
senses.exampleCN: 那名匪徒在码头一带经营保护费生意。
senses.why: Gang first meant a band of people going together, and the suffix -ster marks the person who belongs to it.
senses.whyCN: gang 原指「一起走的一伙人」，后缀 -ster 标记属于这一伙的那个人。

senses.title: A violent professional criminal
senses.definition: a criminal who makes violence his trade, often carrying a weapon
senses.definitionCN: 以暴力为业、常携带武器的罪犯
senses.example: A gangster shot the guard during the robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 抢劫中一名歹徒开枪打伤了警卫。
senses.why: The American coinage tied the word to armed city gangs, so violence became part of its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 美国英语造出这个词时把它与持枪的城市团伙绑在一起，暴力因此进入词义。

senses.title: A ruthless operator in business or politics
senses.definition: a person who uses bullying or dishonest methods to gain power, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用胁迫或不诚实手段夺取权力的人
senses.example: The gangster in the boardroom crushed every rival deal.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会里那个霸道人物扼杀了每一笔竞争交易。
senses.why: Once the criminal image is borrowed, any ruthless exercise of power can be called gangster tactics.
senses.whyCN: 一旦借走罪犯的意象，任何冷酷弄权都可以称为黑帮手段。

senses.title: Used before a noun for the genre
senses.definition: placed before another noun to describe films, music, or stories about gangsters
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，描述以黑帮为题材的电影、音乐或故事
senses.example: The gangster film became a Hollywood staple in the nineteen thirties.
senses.exampleCN: 黑帮电影在二十世纪三十年代成了好莱坞的常见类型。
senses.why: A noun that names a vivid social type easily turns into a label for the stories told about that type.
senses.whyCN: 一个描绘鲜明社会类型的名词，很容易转成为这类故事贴标签的定语。

intro.en: Gangster is a home-grown English compound: the old noun gang plus the agent suffix -ster, coined in American cities.
intro.cn: gangster 是英语本土造的复合词：古老名词 gang 加上施事后缀 -ster，产生于美国城市。

items.en: Gang meant a going or a group of people going together, from the verb gangan, to go.
items.cn: 古英语 gang 意为「行走」或「一起走的一群人」，源自动词 gangan（走）。

items.en: Gang keeps the sense of a band or company, often a neutral one.
items.cn: 中古英语 gang 保留「一伙人、一队人」的意思，常为中性。

items.en: The suffix -ster, once a feminine agent ending, broadens into a general agent suffix.
items.cn: 后缀 -ster 原为阴性施事后缀，十六世纪起扩展为一般施事后缀。

items.en: Gangster is coined for the member of a big-city criminal gang.
items.cn: gangster 在十九世纪九十年代被造出来，指大城市犯罪团伙的成员。

items.en: The word spreads to films, rap, and descriptions of ruthless business conduct.
items.cn: 该词扩展到电影、说唱，以及对不择手段的商业行为的描述。

note.en: Gangster sits at the centre of a small family of gang words and a large field of criminal nouns.
note.cn: gangster 处在一小组 gang 词族的中心，也处在一片广大的罪犯名词义场中。

entries.definition: a group of people who go together, often with criminal aims
entries.definitionCN: 一起行动的一伙人，常指犯罪团伙

entries.definition: the world or territory of criminal gangs
entries.definitionCN: 黑帮的世界或地盘

entries.definition: the methods and culture of gangsters
entries.definitionCN: 黑帮的行事方式与作风

entries.definition: a member of an organized criminal group
entries.definitionCN: 有组织犯罪集团的成员；暴徒

entries.definition: a violent young criminal
entries.definitionCN: 年轻暴徒；小流氓

entries.definition: a person who has committed a crime
entries.definitionCN: 罪犯；犯罪者，范围比 gangster 宽

normalIntro.en: Gangster is gang plus the person suffix -ster, a word born in American crime reporting.
normalIntro.cn: gangster 是 gang 加上表示人的后缀 -ster，诞生于美国犯罪新闻的报道里。

normal.en: Gang plus -ster: the suffix marks the person, as in mobster and prankster.
normal.cn: Gang 加 -ster：后缀标记那个人，mobster 与 prankster 也是这样构词。

normal.en: Gang itself once meant simply a group going together.
normal.cn: gang 本身原只表示「一起走的一群人」。

normal.en: The word was born in American city crime reporting in the 1890s.
normal.cn: 这个词诞生于十九世纪九十年代的美国城市犯罪报道。

normal.en: A gangster film is a whole genre name in Hollywood.
normal.cn: gangster film 是好莱坞一个完整的类型名称。

normal.en: Gangsterism names both the culture and the method.
normal.cn: gangsterism 既指黑帮文化，也指其行事方法。

abstract.en: See a silent man in a dark coat standing at the end of an alley.
abstract.cn: 想象一个穿深色大衣的沉默男人站在巷子尽头。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a gun being checked before a robbery.
abstract.cn: 听见抢劫前检查枪支的咔哒声。

abstract.en: Picture a boardroom where one man quietly destroys a rival.
abstract.cn: 想象会议室里有个人不动声色地击垮对手。

examples.en: Police arrested the gangster at the border.
examples.cn: 警方在边境逮捕了那名匪徒。

examples.en: The gangsters controlled the docks for years.
examples.cn: 那些黑帮分子控制码头多年。

examples.en: The movie tells the story of a gangster who loses everything.
examples.cn: 这部电影讲述一个失去一切的黑帮人物的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「杠事打」——专在街头「杠事」、动不动就打人，就是匪徒；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 gang（行走、同行的一群人）+ 施事后缀 -ster → 美国英语 gangster（犯罪团伙成员）→ 现代英语扩展为「不择手段的强势人物」。

sensesIntro.en: Gangster begins as the name of a gang member, narrows toward armed violence, then widens into a figure for ruthless power and a film-genre label.
sensesIntro.cn: gangster 先指团伙成员，继而收窄到持枪暴力，最后扩展为冷酷权力的比喻与电影类型标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man in a dark coat collecting money from frightened shopkeepers.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿深色大衣的男人向害怕的店主收钱。

branches.en: Belonging to the band is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 属于这一伙人是字面义项。

branches.en: The armed professional is the hardened centre of the word.
branches.cn: 持枪的职业罪犯是这个词最硬核的部分。

branches.en: Ruthless business power is the borrowed figurative sense.
branches.cn: 商业上的冷酷权力是借来的比喻义。

branches.en: The genre label turns the person into a modifier.
branches.cn: 类型标签把这个人物变成了定语。

branches.en: Violence on screen is what the film label sells.
branches.cn: 银幕上的暴力正是这个电影标签所卖的东西。

intro.en: Gangster is built from two native pieces, the noun gang and the agent suffix -ster, with later compounds such as gangland.
intro.cn: gangster 由两个本土成分构成：名词 gang 与施事后缀 -ster，后来又有了 gangland 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and English throughout, with no Latin ancestor, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词从头到尾是日耳曼语与英语成分，没有拉丁语祖先，因此拉丁同源词表为空。

items.meaning: a going, a band of people
items.example: Gang supplies the group at the heart of gangster.
items.exampleCN: gang 提供了 gangster 核心的那个「团伙」。

items.example: Gangan is the verb behind the noun gang.
items.exampleCN: gangan 是名词 gang 背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ster marks the person in gangster.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ster 在 gangster 中标记那个人。

items.meaning: a member of a criminal gang
items.example: Gangster is the American coinage of the 1890s.
items.exampleCN: gangster 是十九世纪九十年代美国英语的新造词。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms gangsterism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 gangsterism。

items.example: Gangsterism names the culture of organized crime.
items.exampleCN: gangsterism 指有组织犯罪的文化。

items.example: Gangland joins gang with land.
items.exampleCN: gangland 把 gang 与 land 组合起来。

items.example: Mobster is a close cousin built with the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: mobster 是用同一后缀构成的近亲词。

items.example: Hoodlum belongs to the same criminal field.
items.exampleCN: hoodlum 属于同一个罪犯义场。

definition_zh: 装束；服装；外表；给……穿衣
definition_en: clothing of a distinctive kind, especially that worn by a group or profession
core_image: 戏台上的一件旧时代长袍，替人说出身份
scene: 剧场后台，演员换上一身旧时代的衣服，准备登台。The actor appeared in the garb of a medieval merchant.
sceneCN: 这里 garb 是「装束」（第 1 个义项：某个群体或行业特有的服装）；句意：那名演员以中世纪商人的装束出场。

derivatives.zh: 穿着……的；由动词加 -ed 构成的形容词
穿衣；装扮；由动词加 -ing 构成的动名词

senses.title: The distinctive clothing of a group
senses.definition: the special clothing worn by members of a profession, order, or people
senses.definitionCN: 某行业、教团或民族成员所穿的特色服装
senses.example: The monks walked in procession in their black garb.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们穿着黑色装束列队行走。
senses.why: The word began as a name for graceful appearance, and clothing is the most visible way a group displays its identity.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指优雅的外表，而服装正是一个群体展示身份最显眼的方式。

senses.title: Clothing in general, in literary use
senses.definition: clothes considered as a whole, used in a slightly formal or literary tone
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一身衣服，语气稍正式或带文学色彩
senses.example: He changed out of his working garb before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭前他换下了干活时穿的衣服。
senses.why: The older sense of style widened until any set of clothes could be called a garb.
senses.whyCN: 「风格」的旧义逐渐放宽，直到任何一身衣服都能称为 garb。

senses.title: An outward form that hides the truth
senses.definition: an outward appearance or form that something takes on, often to disguise its real nature
senses.definitionCN: 事物呈现的外表或形式，常用来掩盖真实性质
senses.example: The policy came in the garb of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 那项政策披着改革的外衣出台。
senses.why: Because dress can disguise a person, garb naturally extends to anything dressed up as something else.
senses.whyCN: 既然衣着能掩盖一个人的身份，garb 自然引申为任何「打扮成别的东西」的外表。

senses.title: To dress or clothe someone
senses.definition: to put clothes on someone, usually in a literary or descriptive style
senses.definitionCN: 给某人穿上衣服，多用于书面或描写性文字
senses.example: She garbed herself in a plain grey dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿上一身素灰色连衣裙。
senses.why: The noun for a whole outfit turned into a verb meaning to put such an outfit on.
senses.whyCN: 指整套装束的名词，转成了「穿上这套装束」的动词。

intro.en: Garb came through Italian and Old French from a Germanic word for equipment; the sense shifted from graceful appearance to clothing.
intro.cn: garb 经意大利语与古法语来自日耳曼语中表示「装备」的词，词义从「优雅外表」转向「服装」。

items.en: A reconstructed garwja-, meaning prepared or equipped, may lie behind the later words for dress.
items.cn: 重构形式 garwja- 意为「准备好的、装备好的」，可能是后来这些「衣着」词的远祖。

items.en: Garwi means preparation or equipment, and it is related to English gear.
items.cn: 古高地德语 garwi 意为准备或装备，与英语 gear 同源。

items.en: Garbo develops the sense of elegance and graceful appearance.
items.cn: 意大利语 garbo 发展出优雅、仪态优美的意思。

items.en: Garbe carries the sense of style or graceful appearance into French.
items.cn: 古法语 garbe 把「风格、优雅外表」的意思带入法语。

items.en: Garb enters English as style or fashion, and quickly also means the clothes that express it.
items.cn: 十六世纪 garb 进入英语，指风格或时尚，很快也指表达这种风格的服装。

items.en: The verb to clothe appears, and the phrase in the garb of extends the word to disguise.
items.cn: 表示「给……穿衣」的动词出现，短语 in the garb of 又把词义扩展到「伪装」。

note.en: Garb has few true relatives in English, so its look-alike list mixes one derived form with two unrelated spellings.
note.cn: garb 在英语里真正的同族词很少，所以形近组里混入一个派生形式与两个无关的拼写近邻。

entries.definition: dressed, usually in a stated way
entries.definitionCN: 穿着……的；garb 的过去分词作形容词

entries.definition: to distort a message or text
entries.definitionCN: 歪曲信息或文字；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an item of clothing
entries.definitionCN: 一件衣服；与 garb 拼写相近，但词源不同

entries.definition: clothing, especially fine or formal clothing
entries.definitionCN: 服装，尤指讲究或正式的衣着

entries.definition: the things people wear
entries.definitionCN: 衣服的总称，语气比 garb 中性

entries.definition: a set of clothes for a role, period, or occasion
entries.definitionCN: 戏服；某个角色、时代或场合穿的整套服装

normalIntro.en: Garb is a dress word with a Germanic equipment word inside it, and it survives mostly in formal and literary phrases.
normalIntro.cn: garb 是个「服装」词，内部藏着日耳曼语表示装备的词，如今多出现在正式与书面短语里。

normal.en: Garb may be related to gear: both go back to a Germanic word for equipment.
normal.cn: garb 可能与 gear 同源：两者都可追溯到日耳曼语表示装备的词。

normal.en: Garb began as a word for style, then shifted to the clothes that show style.
normal.cn: garb 最初指风格，后来转指体现风格的服装。

normal.en: Monks, judges, and graduates all wear a distinctive garb.
normal.cn: 修士、法官与毕业生都穿有辨识度的装束。

normal.en: In the garb of is a formal way to say disguised as.
normal.cn: in the garb of 是「伪装成」的正式说法。

normal.en: The verb is mostly literary: a person is garbed in something.
normal.cn: 动词多用于书面语：某人 garbed in 某物，意即穿着某物。

abstract.en: See a row of monks in dark robes walking in silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一排穿深色长袍的修士默默行走。

abstract.en: Picture a worker changing out of dusty clothes into a clean shirt.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工人脱下满是灰尘的衣服，换上干净衬衫。

abstract.en: Think of an old report wearing the costume of a new reform.
abstract.cn: 想象一份旧报告披着新政的外衣重新出场。

examples.en: The monks wore their traditional garb.
examples.cn: 修士们穿着他们的传统装束。

examples.en: She garbed herself in a plain grey dress.
examples.cn: 她穿上一身素灰色连衣裙。

examples.en: A judge in full garb entered the hall.
examples.cn: 一位身着全套法袍的法官走进大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘎布」——旧戏台上「嘎」的一声拉开幕「布」，演员一身长袍登场；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为由古高地德语 garwi（装备、准备，与 gear 同源）经意大利语 garbo（优雅）与古法语 garbe（优雅外表）进入英语，成为 garb（装束；给……穿衣），核心义「表明身份的穿戴」。

sensesIntro.en: Garb moves from a group uniform to clothes in general, then to any outward disguise, and finally to the act of dressing.
sensesIntro.cn: garb 从群体制服走到泛指衣服，再走成任何外在伪装，最后落到「给……穿衣」的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a robe that tells strangers who the wearer is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件让陌生人看出穿戴者身份的长袍。

branches.en: The uniform of a group is the clearest literal sense.
branches.cn: 群体的制服是最清晰的字面义项。

branches.en: Everyday clothes are the widened literary sense.
branches.cn: 日常衣服是放宽后的书面义项。

branches.en: Outward disguise is the figurative branch.
branches.cn: 外在伪装是比喻分支。

branches.en: The verb turns the outfit into an action.
branches.cn: 动词把整套装束变成动作。

branches.en: Dress both reveals an identity and can hide one.
branches.cn: 服装既透露身份，也能掩盖身份。

intro.en: Garb is short and old, with a Germanic equipment word at its base and a small English family built on it.
intro.cn: garb 短小而古老，底层是日耳曼语表示装备的词，英语围绕它构成了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: The route runs through Italian and Old French, but no Latin etymon is recorded, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经意大利语与古法语传来，但没有记录到拉丁语词源，因此拉丁同源词表为空。

items.example: Garwi is the Germanic base of the dress word.
items.exampleCN: garwi 是这个服装词的日耳曼语基础。

items.example: Italian garbo adds the sense of grace.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 garbo 增添了优雅的含义。

items.example: Old French garbe carries the word toward dress.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 garbe 把这个词引向服装。

items.example: Garb names a whole outfit.
items.exampleCN: garb 指整套装束。

items.example: The verb garb is mostly literary.
items.exampleCN: 动词 garb 多用于书面语。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms garbed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 garbed。

items.example: Garbed describes how a person is dressed.
items.exampleCN: garbed 描述一个人的穿着。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms garbing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 garbing。

items.example: Gear is a Germanic cousin of garb.
items.exampleCN: gear 是 garb 的日耳曼语近亲。

definition_zh: 量具；计量器；标准；尺度；测量；估算；轨距；口径
definition_en: an instrument that measures and shows the amount or level of something
core_image: 表盘上那根指针停在一个刻度上
scene: 机舱里，值班员盯着仪表，确认压力没有超出安全范围。He tapped the gauge and wrote down the reading.
sceneCN: 这里 gauge 是「计量器」（第 1 个义项：测量并显示数值的仪表）；句意：他轻敲计量器，记下了读数。

derivatives.zh: 计量员；测量者；由 gauge 加 -er 构成
可测量的；可估量的；由 gauge 加 -able 构成
测量；计量；由动词加 -ing 构成的动名词

senses.title: An instrument that shows a measurement
senses.definition: a device with a dial or scale that shows the amount or level of something
senses.definitionCN: 带有表盘或刻度、显示某物数量或水平的装置
senses.example: The engineer checked the pressure gauge twice.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了两次压力表。
senses.why: The word first named a measuring rod, and a modern dial is simply a rod turned into a pointer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指量杆，而现代的表盘不过是把杆子变成了指针。

senses.title: To measure an amount
senses.definition: to measure the size, amount, or level of something with an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器测出某物的大小、数量或水平
senses.example: They gauged the depth of the river before building the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 建桥之前他们测量了河水的深度。
senses.why: The verb is the action performed with the instrument, so the tool and its use share one form.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是用这件仪器完成的动作，工具与用法因此共用一个词形。

senses.title: To judge feelings or opinions
senses.definition: to form an opinion about what people think or feel, without exact measurement
senses.definitionCN: 在没有精确测量的情况下，对人们的想法或感受作出判断
senses.example: It is hard to gauge how angry she really is.
senses.exampleCN: 很难判断她到底有多生气。
senses.why: Measuring gives a reading of quantity, and judging gives a reading of mood; the metaphor transfers the dial to people.
senses.whyCN: 测量给出数量的读数，判断给出情绪的读数；这个比喻把表盘移到了人身上。

senses.title: A standard for comparison
senses.definition: a fact or figure used as a standard when judging something else
senses.definitionCN: 用来评判其他事物的标准或数据
senses.example: Test scores are only one gauge of a school.
senses.exampleCN: 考试成绩只是衡量一所学校的标准之一。
senses.why: A gauge was also the fixed standard of measure, so anything that sets the scale can be called a gauge.
senses.whyCN: gauge 也曾指固定的计量标准，因此任何设定尺度的事物都能叫 gauge。

senses.title: The width between railway rails
senses.definition: the distance between the two rails of a railway track
senses.definitionCN: 铁路两条钢轨之间的距离
senses.example: The narrow gauge railway climbs steeply.
senses.exampleCN: 那条窄轨铁路爬坡很陡。
senses.why: Railway engineers needed a word for the fixed spacing of rails, and the standard measure sense supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 铁路工程师需要给钢轨的固定间距取个名字，而「计量标准」的义项正好提供了它。

senses.title: The bore of a gun or the thickness of wire
senses.definition: the internal diameter of a gun barrel, or the diameter of wire or sheet metal
senses.definitionCN: 枪管内径，或金属丝、金属板的直径与厚度
senses.example: A twelve gauge shotgun fires a heavy load.
senses.exampleCN: 十二号口径的猎枪发射很重的弹丸。
senses.why: Technical trades measure bores and wires by diameter, so the name of the measuring tool became the name of the size.
senses.whyCN: 技术行业按直径测量枪管与金属丝，量具之名便成了尺寸之名。

intro.en: The origin of gauge is uncertain: it is generally traced to a Frankish word for a pole, through Old North French.
intro.cn: gauge 的词源不确定：一般认为它来自法兰克语表示「杆」的词，经古北法语传入。

items.en: A reconstructed galga, a pole or rod, is often proposed as the source.
items.cn: 重构形式 galga（杆、棒）常被提出来作为词源。

items.en: Gauge names a measuring rod or a standard of measure.
items.cn: gauge 指量杆或计量标准。

items.en: Gauge appears early in the fifteenth century as a fixed standard of measure.
items.cn: gauge 在十五世纪初出现，指固定的计量标准。

items.en: By the 1680s a gauge is an instrument that shows a reading.
items.cn: 到十七世纪八十年代，gauge 指能显示读数的仪表。

items.en: Railway engineers give it the sense of track width in the 1840s.
items.cn: 十九世纪四十年代，铁路工程师赋予它「轨距」的含义。

items.en: The verb extends from measuring things to judging moods and opinions.
items.cn: 动词从测量物体扩展到判断情绪与民意。

note.en: Gauge has a twin spelling, a small derived family, and a wide field of measuring words around it.
note.cn: gauge 有一个孪生拼写、一个小的派生词族，周围还有一整片表示测量的词。

entries.definition: an alternative spelling of gauge, common in American usage
entries.definitionCN: gauge 的另一种拼写，在美国用法中常见；作「抵押品」讲时另有词源

entries.definition: a person who measures, especially a tax officer
entries.definitionCN: 计量员；尤指负责计量的税务人员

entries.definition: the act of measuring
entries.definitionCN: 测量的动作；由动词 gauge 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: to find the size or amount of something
entries.definitionCN: 测量；量出大小或数量，是最通用的说法

entries.definition: a device that measures and records an amount
entries.definitionCN: 计量表；记录用量的装置

entries.definition: a standard by which something is judged
entries.definitionCN: 标准；准则，与「尺度」义项最接近

normalIntro.en: Gauge is a measuring word that moves easily from a dial to a judgment, and it has a twin spelling, gage.
normalIntro.cn: gauge 是个测量词，能从表盘轻松滑向判断，还有一个孪生拼写 gage。

normal.en: Gauge and gage are two spellings of one word, and the verb keeps gauge.
normal.cn: gauge 与 gage 是同一个词的两种拼写，动词一般仍写 gauge。

normal.en: A gauge turns an invisible quantity into a pointer on a dial.
normal.cn: gauge 把看不见的数量变成表盘上的一根指针。

normal.en: Pressure gauge, fuel gauge, rain gauge: the pattern is a noun plus gauge.
normal.cn: 「pressure gauge」「fuel gauge」「rain gauge」都是名词加 gauge 的模式。

normal.en: To gauge a mood is to read it the way a dial reads pressure.
normal.cn: 揣测情绪，就像表盘读取压力那样去「读」它。

normal.en: Railway gauge measures the width between rails, not the length of the line.
normal.cn: 轨距量的是两根钢轨之间的宽度，不是线路的长度。

abstract.en: See a needle trembling just below the red zone.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针在红色区域下方微微颤动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a rod against a wall to mark a height.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把杆子抵在墙上，标出一个高度。

abstract.en: Think of reading a room the moment you walk in.
abstract.cn: 想象你走进房间的一瞬间就读懂了气氛。

examples.en: The engineer checked the pressure gauge twice.
examples.cn: 工程师检查了两次压力表。

examples.en: It is hard to gauge how angry she really is.
examples.cn: 很难判断她到底有多生气。

examples.en: The narrow gauge railway climbs steeply.
examples.cn: 那条窄轨铁路爬坡很陡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给治」——仪表「给」出读数，工人据此「治」理机器；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自法兰克语 galga（杆、棒）→ 古北法语 gauge（量杆、计量标准）→ 中古英语 gauge → 现代英语 gauge（量具；测量；判断），核心义「用一根标尺量出多少」。

sensesIntro.en: Gauge starts as a measuring rod, becomes the instrument and the standard, then the act of measuring and the judgment that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: gauge 从量杆起步，变成仪器与标准，再变成测量的动作，最后延伸到由此作出的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pointer resting on a marked scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根指针停在有刻度的标尺上。

branches.en: The dial instrument is the everyday literal sense.
branches.cn: 表盘仪器是日常的字面义项。

branches.en: The measuring action is the verb built on the tool.
branches.cn: 测量动作是建立在工具之上的动词。

branches.en: Judging a mood is the figurative reading.
branches.cn: 判断情绪是比喻性的「读数」。

branches.en: A standard is the older sense of a fixed measure.
branches.cn: 标准是「固定尺度」这一较古老的义项。

branches.en: Rail width and bore size are technical dimensions.
branches.cn: 轨距与口径都是技术性的尺寸。

intro.en: Gauge is a short measuring word with a small English family and a twin spelling, gage.
intro.cn: gauge 是个简短的测量词，有一个小小的英语词族，还有一个孪生拼写 gage。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recorded for gauge; the chain runs from Frankish through Old North French, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: gauge 没有记录到拉丁语词源；词源链从法兰克语经古北法语而来，因此拉丁同源词表为空。

items.example: Galga is the proposed root of the measuring word.
items.exampleCN: galga 是这个测量词被提出的词根。

items.example: Old North French gauge already means a measure.
items.exampleCN: 古北法语 gauge 已经表示计量标准。

items.example: Middle English gauge fixes the standard sense.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语 gauge 固定了「标准」这一义项。

items.example: The modern gauge shows a reading on a dial.
items.exampleCN: 现代 gauge 在表盘上显示读数。

items.example: The verb gauge covers both measuring and judging.
items.exampleCN: 动词 gauge 兼指测量与判断。

items.example: The suffix -er forms gauger.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 gauger。

items.example: A gauger checks the contents of a cask.
items.exampleCN: 计量员检查桶内装了多少。

items.example: The suffix -able forms gaugeable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 gaugeable。

items.example: Gaugeable means able to be measured.
items.exampleCN: gaugeable 意为可以测量。

definition_zh: 凝胶；胶状物；发胶；胶化；磨合
definition_en: a thick jelly-like substance, especially one used on hair or skin or in technical products
core_image: 一勺半透明的胶状物，挂在勺背上不肯流下
scene: 美发店里，造型师把透明胶状物抹在客人头发上，再用梳子定型。A thin layer of gel kept the curls in place all evening.
sceneCN: 这里 gel 是「凝胶」（第 1 个义项：抹在头发或皮肤上的胶状物）；句意：薄薄一层凝胶让卷发整晚都保持形状。

derivatives.zh: 明胶；由拉丁语 gelatus 经法语进入英语
胶状的；黏稠的；由 gelatin 加 -ous 构成
胶化；凝胶化过程；由 gel 加 -ation 构成

senses.title: A jelly-like product for hair or skin
senses.definition: a thick transparent jelly-like substance sold for use on hair, skin, or nails
senses.definitionCN: 浓稠透明的胶状物，用于头发、皮肤或指甲
senses.example: She put gel in her hair before the party.
senses.exampleCN: 参加聚会前她在头发上抹了发胶。
senses.why: The word is a clipping of gelatin, and the first everyday product to borrow the name was hair gel.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 gelatin（明胶）的缩写，最早借用这个名字的日用品就是发胶。

senses.title: A semi-solid colloid in chemistry
senses.definition: a colloid in which a solid network holds liquid, giving a semi-solid state
senses.definitionCN: 固体网络兜住液体的胶体，呈半固态
senses.example: The laboratory stored the sample in a silica gel.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把样品保存在硅胶里。
senses.why: Gelatin sets into exactly this state, so chemists took the short word for the whole class of colloids.
senses.whyCN: 明胶正好凝固成这种状态，化学家便用这个短词来称呼整类胶体。

senses.title: To set into a jelly
senses.definition: to become a gel, or to make a liquid set into a jelly-like state
senses.definitionCN: 变成凝胶，或使液体凝固成胶状
senses.example: The mixture will gel in about an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种混合物大约一小时后会胶化。
senses.why: The noun names the state, and the verb names the change into that state.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名那种状态，动词命名进入那种状态的变化。

senses.title: To mesh and take shape
senses.definition: of people, plans, or ideas, to work well together and begin to take definite shape
senses.definitionCN: 指人、计划或想法彼此契合，开始成形
senses.example: The new team gelled after a few weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 新团队几周后就磨合好了。
senses.why: Loose parts that set into a gel stop sliding, and a group that gels behaves the same way.
senses.whyCN: 松散的成分凝成凝胶后不再滑动，磨合好的团队也是这样。

senses.title: To apply gel to hair
senses.definition: to put gel on hair in order to shape or hold it
senses.definitionCN: 把凝胶涂在头发上以定型或固定
senses.example: He gelled his hair before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前他用发胶定了型。
senses.why: The product name turned into the verb for using the product, a very common English shift.
senses.whyCN: 产品名称转成使用该产品的动词，这是英语里很常见的转化。

intro.en: Gel is a modern clipping of gelatin, whose root is Latin gelare, to freeze; the whole family goes back to cold.
intro.cn: gel 是 gelatin（明胶）的现代缩写，其词根是拉丁语 gelare（冻结），整族词都回到「寒冷」。

items.en: Gelu means frost or intense cold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gelu 意为霜或严寒。

items.en: Gelare means to freeze or to make stiff.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gelare 意为冻结或使变硬。

items.en: The participle gelatus means frozen or stiffened.
items.cn: 分词 gelatus 意为冻住的、变硬的。

items.en: French gélatine and English gelatin name the substance made from boiled animal parts.
items.cn: 法语 gélatine 与英语 gelatin 指用动物原料熬煮制成的明胶。

items.en: Gel appears as a short form for gelatin, used for cosmetic and technical products.
items.cn: gel 在 1899 年作为 gelatin 的缩写出现，用于化妆品与技术产品。

items.en: The verb gel grows from setting liquids to groups and plans that mesh.
items.cn: 动词 gel 从液体的凝固，扩展到团队与计划的磨合。

note.en: Gel is the short modern member of a Latin family, standing beside gelatin words and jelly-like materials.
note.cn: gel 是拉丁词族里现代出现的短词，旁边是 gelatin 一族与各种胶状材料。

entries.definition: a clear substance made by boiling animal bones and skin
entries.definitionCN: 明胶；由动物骨皮熬煮而成的透明胶质，是 gel 的全称来源

entries.definition: thick and jelly-like
entries.definitionCN: 胶状的；黏稠的

entries.definition: the process of becoming a gel
entries.definitionCN: 胶化；凝胶化过程

entries.definition: a soft wobbling food or substance made with gelatin
entries.definitionCN: 果冻；柔软晃动的胶状食物，与 gel 同源

entries.definition: a substance with tiny particles spread through another substance
entries.definitionCN: 胶体；微粒分散在另一物质中的体系

entries.definition: a soft wet mixture that can be spread
entries.definitionCN: 糊状物；可以涂抹的柔软湿混合物

normalIntro.en: Gel is a clipped gelatin word: Latin cold, French jelly, and English hair product all in four letters.
normalIntro.cn: gel 是缩写而来的 gelatin 词：拉丁语的寒冷、法语的胶质、英语的发胶，都压缩在四个字母里。

normal.en: Gel is a clipping of gelatin, which comes from Latin gelare, to freeze.
normal.cn: gel 是 gelatin 的缩写，而 gelatin 来自拉丁语 gelare（冻结）。

normal.en: Hair gel, shower gel: the pattern is a noun plus gel.
normal.cn: 「hair gel」「shower gel」都是名词加 gel 的模式。

normal.en: A gel sits between a liquid and a solid.
normal.cn: 凝胶处在液体与固体之间。

normal.en: When a plan gels, its parts stop sliding and hold together.
normal.cn: 计划「成形」时，各个部分不再滑动，而是扣合在一起。

normal.en: The doubled l in gelled and gelling keeps the short vowel.
normal.cn: gelled 与 gelling 里双写的 l 是为了保持短元音。

abstract.en: See a swirl of blue gel inside a glass jar.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃罐里一团打旋的蓝色凝胶。

abstract.en: Picture a beaker where the liquid suddenly refuses to flow.
abstract.cn: 想象烧杯里的液体突然不肯流动了。

abstract.en: Watch a sauce thicken until it holds its shape on a spoon.
abstract.cn: 看着酱汁变稠，直到能在勺子上立住形状。

examples.en: She put gel in her hair before the party.
examples.cn: 参加聚会前她在头发上抹了发胶。

examples.en: The mixture will gel in about an hour.
examples.cn: 这种混合物大约一小时后会胶化。

examples.en: The new team gelled after a few weeks.
examples.cn: 新团队几周后就磨合好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胶」——读音像中文的「胶」，意思正好也是胶状物；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gelu（霜、寒冷）→ gelare（冻结）→ gelatus（冻住的）→ 法语 gélatine 与英语 gelatin（明胶）→ 美式英语 gel（凝胶），核心义「冻住而半凝的胶状物」。

sensesIntro.en: Gel begins as a short name for a cosmetic and technical substance, then names the setting action and finally the meshing of people or plans.
sensesIntro.cn: gel 先是化妆品与技术用胶状物的简称，随后指凝固动作，最后指人与计划的磨合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoonful of clear jelly that will not pour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺倒不出来的透明胶状物。

branches.en: The everyday cosmetic product is the first sense.
branches.cn: 日常化妆品是最先出现的义项。

branches.en: The chemical colloid is the technical widening.
branches.cn: 化学胶体是技术性的扩展。

branches.en: Setting into a jelly is the verbal action.
branches.cn: 凝成胶状是动词性的动作。

branches.en: A group that meshes borrows the image of setting jelly.
branches.cn: 磨合好的团队借用了胶体凝固的意象。

branches.en: The product and the act of applying it share one word.
branches.cn: 产品与使用产品的动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Gel is short, but the family behind it is Latin and large: gelatin, gelatinous, and gelation all grow from the same root.
intro.cn: gel 很短，但背后的词族来自拉丁语且很庞大：gelatin、gelatinous 与 gelation 都长在同一个词根上。
