latinIntro.en: Latin gelu and gelare supply the freezing image, and gelatus supplies the participle behind gelatin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gelu 与 gelare 提供「冻结」的意象，gelatus 则提供 gelatin 背后的分词形式。

items.example: Gelu gives the family its cold image.
items.exampleCN: gelu 给这个词族带来「寒冷」的意象。

items.example: Gelare is the verb behind gel and gelatin.
items.exampleCN: gelare 是 gel 与 gelatin 背后的动词。

items.example: Gelatus leads toward the word gelatin.
items.exampleCN: gelatus 通向了 gelatin 这个词。

items.example: French gélatine carries the Latin root into modern use.
items.exampleCN: 法语 gélatine 把拉丁词根带进现代用法。

items.example: Gelatin is the full word that gel clips.
items.exampleCN: gelatin 是 gel 缩写所依据的全称。

items.example: Gel is the short modern form.
items.exampleCN: gel 是现代的短形式。

items.example: The verb gel covers setting and meshing.
items.exampleCN: 动词 gel 兼指凝固与磨合。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 表示「充满……的、具有……性质的」
items.example: The suffix -ous forms gelatinous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 gelatinous。

items.example: Gelatinous describes a jelly-like texture.
items.exampleCN: gelatinous 描述胶状的质地。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms gelation.

definition_zh: 明胶；动物胶；胶质食品
definition_en: a clear protein made from animal collagen, used to make foods set, or a food made with it
core_image: 一碗放凉的肉汤表面凝成颤动的透明胶层
scene: 厨房里，煮过骨头的高汤在冰箱里放了一夜，表面凝成一层颤动的胶。Overnight in the fridge, the bone broth turned into a firm layer of gelatin.
sceneCN: 这里 gelatin 是「明胶」（第 1 个义项：从动物胶原煮出的胶质）；句意：高汤在冰箱里放了一夜，凝成一层坚实的明胶。

derivatives.zh: 胶状的；像明胶一样黏软的
使胶化；把液体变成胶状
凝胶；胶体，由 gelatin 逆构而来的短形式

senses.title: The setting protein
senses.definition: a clear protein obtained by boiling animal bones, skin, and connective tissue, used to make foods set
senses.definitionCN: 熬煮动物骨、皮与结缔组织得到的透明蛋白质，用来使食物凝固
senses.example: The marshmallows contain pork gelatin.
senses.exampleCN: 这些棉花糖含有猪明胶。
senses.why: Gelatin goes back to Latin gelatus, frozen or stiffened, because boiled collagen turns firm as it cools.
senses.whyCN: gelatin 源自拉丁语 gelatus（冻结、变硬），因为煮过的胶原冷却后会凝成固体。

senses.title: A jelly-like food
senses.definition: a sweet food made with gelatin, fruit juice, and sugar that shakes when it is moved
senses.definitionCN: 用明胶、果汁和糖做成的甜食，移动时会颤动
senses.example: The children were given fruit gelatin for dessert.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们甜点吃的是水果果冻。
senses.why: Once the protein sets, it can hold a flavoured liquid in a soft, wobbling shape, and that became a food of its own.
senses.whyCN: 蛋白质凝固后能把调味液体固定成柔软颤动的形状，于是自成一类食品。

senses.title: The film coating
senses.definition: a thin layer of gelatin used to hold light-sensitive chemicals on photographic film
senses.definitionCN: 摄影胶片上用来固定感光化学物质的薄明胶层
senses.example: Old film relies on a gelatin layer to keep its silver salts in place.
senses.exampleCN: 老式胶片靠一层明胶把银盐固定住。
senses.why: Because gelatin forms a stable, transparent sheet, early photography used it as the base for light-sensitive emulsions.
senses.whyCN: 因为明胶能形成稳定透明的薄片，早期摄影便用它作为感光乳剂的载体。

intro.en: Gelatin reached English through French and Italian from Latin gelatus, meaning frozen or stiffened.
intro.cn: gelatin 经法语和意大利语进入英语，源头是拉丁语 gelatus，意为「冻结的、变硬的」。

items.en: Gelare means to freeze or make stiff.
items.cn: gelare 意为冻结、使变硬。

items.en: Gelatus, its past participle, means frozen or set.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 gelatus 意为冻结的、凝固的。

items.en: Gelatina names a jelly-like substance.
items.cn: gelatina 指胶状物质。

items.en: Gelatine enters French as the name of the edible substance.
items.cn: gelatine 在法语中成为这种食用胶质的名称。

items.en: English borrows gelatin in the eighteenth century for kitchen and laboratory use.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 gelatin，供厨房与实验室使用。

note.en: Gelatin belongs to a cold-setting word family: jelly, gel, and gelatinous all share the image of collagen turning firm.
note.cn: gelatin 属于「冷凝」词族：jelly、gel 与 gelatinous 都共享胶原凝固的意象。

entries.definition: the British spelling of gelatin
entries.definitionCN: gelatin 的英式拼写，词源相同

entries.definition: thick and sticky like jelly
entries.definitionCN: 胶状的；像果冻一样黏软的

entries.definition: a soft, semi-solid substance
entries.definitionCN: 凝胶；胶体，由 gelatin 逆构而来的短词

entries.definition: a soft, transparent food made by boiling fruit with sugar
entries.definitionCN: 果冻；水果熬成的透明甜食

entries.definition: the protein in skin and bone from which gelatin is made
entries.definitionCN: 胶原蛋白，是制取明胶的原料

entries.definition: a jelly-like substance from seaweed used instead of gelatin
entries.definitionCN: 琼脂，从海藻提取的明胶替代品

normalIntro.en: Gelatin is frozen softness: warm liquid collagen becomes a firm, shaking sheet when it cools.
normalIntro.cn: gelatin 是「冻住的柔软」：温热的胶原液体冷却后变成颤动的固体薄片。

normal.en: Think of gel plus in: a gel that has been stabilised into a food ingredient.
normal.cn: 记作 gel 加 in：一种被稳定下来的凝胶食材。

normal.en: Gelatin powder dissolves in hot water and sets as it cools.
normal.cn: 明胶粉在热水中溶解，冷却后凝固。

normal.en: Gelatinous describes anything with that wobbly jelly texture.
normal.cn: gelatinous 形容一切如果冻般颤动的质地。

normal.en: Photographic film kept its silver salts inside a gelatin layer.
normal.cn: 摄影胶片把银盐保存在明胶层里。

normal.en: Compare jelly: jelly is the fruity food, gelatin is the protein that makes it set.
normal.cn: 对比 jelly：jelly 是水果甜点，gelatin 是让它凝固的蛋白质。

abstract.en: Picture a steaming pot of bone broth going still and glassy overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅热气腾腾的骨汤过夜后变得静止而透明。

abstract.en: See a plate of red fruit jelly trembling when the table is tapped.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘红色水果果冻在桌子被碰时轻轻颤动。

abstract.en: Imagine a strip of film dipped in warm liquid that dries into a clear coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条胶片浸过温热的液体，晾干后留下一层透明薄膜。

examples.en: Gelatin is made by boiling collagen from animal bones and skin.
examples.cn: 明胶由熬煮动物骨皮中的胶原制成。

examples.en: She dissolved a spoonful of gelatin in hot water before adding the juice.
examples.cn: 她先把一勺明胶溶于热水，再加入果汁。

examples.en: The old photographs were printed on glass plates coated with gelatin.
examples.cn: 那些老照片印在涂有明胶的玻璃板上。

root: 拉丁语 gelare（冻结）→ gelatus（冻住的）→ 意大利语 gelatina → 法语 gelatine → 英语 gelatin，核心义「胶原煮后冷凝成的胶」。

sensesIntro.en: Gelatin starts as the protein itself, then the sweet food made from it, and finally the transparent coating that photography borrowed from the kitchen.
sensesIntro.cn: gelatin 先指蛋白质本身，再指用它做的甜点，最后指摄影从厨房借去的透明涂层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm liquid that cools into a clear, trembling sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：温热的液体冷却成一层透明颤动的薄片。

branches.en: The protein sense names the substance itself.
branches.cn: 蛋白质义项指这种物质本身。

branches.en: The dessert sense turns the substance into a familiar food.
branches.cn: 甜点义项把这种物质变成熟悉的食品。

branches.en: The photographic sense uses its clear setting power.
branches.cn: 摄影义项利用它透明凝固的特性。

branches.en: A jelly on the table is the protein made visible and sweet.
branches.cn: 桌上的果冻就是看得见、变甜了的明胶。

branches.en: Both the kitchen block and the film coat are set collagen.
branches.cn: 厨房里的胶块与胶片涂层都是凝固的胶原。

intro.en: Gelatin is built on the Latin freezing root gel-, with gel, gelatinous, and gelatinize around it.
intro.cn: gelatin 建立在拉丁语「冻结」词根 gel- 上，周围有 gel、gelatinous 与 gelatinize。

latinIntro.en: Latin gelare means to freeze, and gelatus means frozen or stiffened.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gelare 意为冻结，gelatus 意为冻住的、变硬的。

items.example: Gelare supplies the freezing idea.
items.exampleCN: gelare 提供「冻结」这一概念。

items.example: Gelatus is the past participle behind the name.
items.exampleCN: gelatus 是名称背后的过去分词。

items.example: Italian gelatina named the jelly first.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 gelatina 最早为这种胶质命名。

items.example: French gelatine carried the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 gelatine 把该词带入英语。

items.meaningCN: 用于物质名称的名词后缀
items.example: The variant gelatine keeps the French -ine ending.
items.exampleCN: 异体拼写 gelatine 保留了法语 -ine 词尾。

items.example: Gel is the short form of the same idea.
items.exampleCN: gel 是同一概念缩短后的形式。

items.example: Gelatinous describes a sticky, trembling texture.
items.exampleCN: gelatinous 形容黏稠颤动的质地。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous turns gelatin into gelatinous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把 gelatin 变成 gelatinous。

items.example: Gelatinize describes the change from liquid to gel.
items.exampleCN: gelatinize 描述从液体变为凝胶的过程。

items.example: The suffix -ize builds verbs such as gelatinize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 gelatinize 这类动词。

definition_zh: 概括；归纳；推广；泛泛而谈
definition_en: to form a general rule from particular cases, or to make something apply more widely
core_image: 从一堆具体事例中抽出一根共同的线
scene: 老师让学生先看三份调查表，再从中总结出一条适用于全班的规律。The teacher asked the class to study three surveys and then generalise a rule that would fit the whole group.
sceneCN: 这里 generalise 是「归纳出一般规律」（第 1 个义项：从个别事例抽出通则）；句意：老师让学生先看三份调查表，再归纳出一条适用于全班的规律。

pos.zh: 概括；归纳；推广；泛泛而谈

derivatives.zh: 概括；通则；推广，由动词加 -ation 构成
笼统的；一般化的，由过去分词转作形容词
通才，由 general 加 -ist 构成
一般性；通则，由 general 加 -ity 构成

senses.title: To draw a general rule
senses.definition: to move from particular facts to a broad statement that covers many of them
senses.definitionCN: 从个别事实转向覆盖许多事实的宽泛结论
senses.example: Researchers generalise from hundreds of individual cases.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者从数百个个别案例中归纳出通则。
senses.why: The base word general names a whole class, so the verb means drawing a whole-class statement out of single examples.
senses.whyCN: 词基 general 指整个类别，所以这个动词表示从单个例子中抽出覆盖整类的说法。

senses.title: To speak without details
senses.definition: to make a broad claim that ignores exceptions and details, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 作出忽略例外与细节的宽泛论断，往往有失公允
senses.example: It is unwise to generalise about a whole nation from one visit.
senses.exampleCN: 只凭一次访问就对整个国家泛泛而谈是不明智的。
senses.why: The same movement upward from details can go too far, producing a claim that skips the exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「从细节向上」的动作一旦走过头，就会得到忽略例外的论断。

senses.title: To extend to a wider field
senses.definition: to take a method, rule, or result and show that it works beyond its first setting
senses.definitionCN: 把方法、规则或结果拿到最初场景之外，证明它仍然有效
senses.example: The team hopes to generalise the treatment to other age groups.
senses.exampleCN: 团队希望把这种疗法推广到其他年龄组。
senses.why: A general rule is one that holds beyond its birthplace, so the verb also means carrying it into new territory.
senses.whyCN: 通则之所以为通则，是因为它超出原产地仍然成立，因此这个动词也指把它带进新领域。

senses.title: To make formally general
senses.definition: in mathematics and logic, to restate a result in a form that covers a whole class of cases
senses.definitionCN: 在数学与逻辑中，把结果改写成覆盖一整类情形的形式
senses.example: Mathematicians generalise a theorem by dropping one restrictive condition.
senses.exampleCN: 数学家去掉一个限制条件，从而把定理一般化。
senses.why: Formal work pushes the everyday meaning to its limit: a statement is rewritten so that a whole class of cases falls under it.
senses.whyCN: 形式化工作把日常含义推到极限：把命题改写，使一整类情形都落入其中。

intro.en: Generalise joins general with the verb suffix -ise; general goes back through French to Latin generalis, from genus, a kind or class.
intro.cn: generalise 由 general 加动词后缀 -ise 构成；general 经法语上溯到拉丁语 generalis，再源于 genus（类别）。

items.en: Genus means kind, stock, or class.
items.cn: genus 意为种类、族类或类别。

items.en: Generalis means belonging to a whole kind or class.
items.cn: generalis 意为属于整个类别的。

items.en: General reaches French as a word for a whole class.
items.cn: general 以「整个类别」之义进入法语。

items.en: English adopts general as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语借入 general，兼作形容词与名词。

items.en: The verb generalise appears in English writing about broad claims.
items.cn: 动词 generalise 在十八世纪英语中表示作出宽泛论断。

items.en: Modern usage adds the sense of extending a method or result to new cases.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了把方法或结果推广到新情形的含义。

note.en: Generalise sits in the genus family: general, generality, and generalisation all turn a class into words.
note.cn: generalise 属于 genus 词族：general、generality 与 generalisation 都把「类别」变成词语。

entries.definition: covering a whole class rather than details
entries.definitionCN: 一般的；总体的，是本词的词基

entries.definition: a broad statement drawn from particular cases
entries.definitionCN: 概括；通则，由动词加名词后缀构成

entries.definition: a person who knows a little about many fields
entries.definitionCN: 通才，词根同为 genus（类别）

entries.definition: to state the main points of something briefly
entries.definitionCN: 总结；概述

entries.definition: to extend a known pattern to unknown cases
entries.definitionCN: 外推；据已知推未知（正式）

entries.definition: to treat a whole group as if every member were the same
entries.definitionCN: 把群体模式化看待；对群体抱刻板印象

normalIntro.en: Generalise is a mental ladder: climb from single cases to the whole class, then check that the top step still holds.
normalIntro.cn: generalise 像一架思维梯子：从单个事例爬到整个类别，再检查最高一级是否仍然站得住。

normal.en: General plus ise: the verb turns a whole class into a statement.
normal.cn: general 加 ise：这个动词把整个类别变成一句话。

normal.en: You generalise from data, and you generalise a rule to new fields.
normal.cn: 从数据出发是归纳，把规则推向新领域是推广。

normal.en: Generalisation is the noun for the broad statement you reach.
normal.cn: generalisation 是你得出的那条宽泛结论的名词形式。

normal.en: A generalist knows many fields and specialises in none.
normal.cn: generalist 了解许多领域，却不专精于任何一门。

normal.en: Compare summarise: summarise condenses what is there, generalise goes beyond it.
normal.cn: 对比 summarise：summarise 压缩已有内容，generalise 则走出已有内容。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling one thread out of a tangle of loose ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从一团乱线中抽出一根线。

abstract.en: See a net thrown so wide that it catches fish it never meant to catch.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网撒得太宽，捞到了本不想捞的鱼。

abstract.en: Imagine a small key that is copied and made to open a whole row of doors.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小钥匙被复制，用来打开一整排门。

examples.en: It is risky to generalise from a single interview.
examples.cn: 仅凭一次访谈就归纳出结论是有风险的。

examples.en: The paper generalises its findings to all similar schools.
examples.cn: 这篇论文把研究结果推广到所有同类学校。

examples.en: Good science generalises slowly and checks each step.
examples.cn: 好的科学慢慢归纳，并逐步检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皆能来事」——从个别事例「皆能」推出一条通则；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 genus（种类、族类）→ generalis（属于整类的）→ 古法语 general → 英语 general → general 加 -ise → generalise，核心义「把个别归入整类」。

sensesIntro.en: Generalise begins with the careful move from cases to a rule, then the careless version of that move, then the deliberate extension of a method, and finally its formal mathematical form.
sensesIntro.cn: generalise 先指从个案谨慎地抽出通则，再指同样动作的草率版本，然后指有意把方法推广，最后指数学与逻辑中的形式化泛化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thread pulled out of a heap of separate cases.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一堆彼此分开的事例中抽出一根共同的线。

branches.en: Drawing a rule from cases is the core sense.
branches.cn: 从个案抽出规则是核心义项。

branches.en: Overreach turns the same move into a careless claim.
branches.cn: 过度延伸把同一动作变成草率论断。

branches.en: Extending a method is the practical sense.
branches.cn: 推广方法是实用义项。

branches.en: Formal generality is the mathematical sense.
branches.cn: 形式化的一般性是数学义项。

branches.en: A sound generalisation can be carried into a new field.
branches.cn: 可靠的概括可以带进新领域。

intro.en: Generalise is built from Latin genus, the class root, through general and the verb suffix -ise.
intro.cn: generalise 由拉丁语 genus（类别）经 general 与动词后缀 -ise 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus means kind or class, and generalis means belonging to a whole class.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genus 意为种类或类别，generalis 意为属于整个类别的。

items.example: Genus is the class root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: genus 是整个词族背后的「类别」词根。

items.example: Generalis gives English the adjective general.
items.exampleCN: generalis 为英语提供了形容词 general。

items.example: Generare shares the same class root.
items.exampleCN: generare 共享同一个「类别」词根。

items.example: Old French general passes the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 general 把该词传给英语。

items.example: General is the base of the verb.
items.exampleCN: general 是这个动词的词基。

items.example: The suffix -ise builds generalise from general.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 由 general 构成 generalise。

items.example: Generalise is the verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: generalise 是这个词族的动词。

items.example: Generalisation names the statement you reach.
items.exampleCN: generalisation 指你得出的那条结论。

items.example: Generality keeps the class meaning.
items.exampleCN: generality 保留「类别」含义。

items.meaning: a person of broad rather than deep knowledge
items.example: Generalist adds -ist to the base.
items.exampleCN: generalist 在词基后加 -ist。

definition_zh: 有生殖能力的；有创造力的；生成的
definition_en: able to produce new life, new ideas, or new forms
core_image: 一粒种子在手里裂开，抽出新的芽
scene: 温室里，一株野草结出成千上万的种子，每一粒都能长成新的植株。In the greenhouse, one wild plant produced thousands of seeds, each of them generative and able to start a new plant.
sceneCN: 这里 generative 是「能繁殖的；有生殖能力的」（第 1 个义项：能产生新个体）；句意：一株野草结出成千上万的种子，每一粒都能长出新植株。

pos.zh: 有生殖能力的；有创造力的；生成的

derivatives.zh: 产生；一代，由 generate 加 -ation 构成
发电机；生成器，由 generate 加 -or 构成
产生；生成，是本词的动词词基

senses.title: Able to produce life
senses.titleCN: 有生殖能力的；能繁殖的
senses.definition: having the power to produce offspring or new living things
senses.definitionCN: 有能力产生后代或新的生物个体
senses.example: Every seed is generative, carrying a whole plant inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 每一粒种子都有生殖能力，内部藏着一整株植物。
senses.why: The Latin root gignere means to beget, so anything generative carries the power to bring new life into being.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gignere 意为生育，因此 generative 指具有把新生命带到世上的能力。

senses.title: Able to produce new ideas
senses.definition: having the power to originate new ideas, forms, or works rather than copy old ones
senses.definitionCN: 有能力创造新的想法、形式或作品，而不是复制旧有之物
senses.example: The studio became a generative force in modern design.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室成为现代设计中的一股创造力量。
senses.why: Begetting extends from bodies to minds: a generative mind gives birth to new thoughts and forms.
senses.whyCN: 「生育」从身体延伸到头脑：有生成力的头脑会孕育新的思想与形式。

senses.title: Describing grammar that generates sentences
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing a finite set of rules that can produce all the sentences of a language
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中形容一套有限规则能产出一种语言的全部句子
senses.example: Generative grammar treats a sentence as the output of rules.
senses.exampleCN: 生成语法把句子看作规则输出的结果。
senses.why: If a small rule set can give birth to endlessly many sentences, the rules themselves deserve the name generative.
senses.whyCN: 如果一套有限的规则能生出无穷多的句子，这套规则本身就该称为「生成的」。

senses.title: Producing data or images by model
senses.definition: in computing, describing a model that creates new text, images, or audio instead of only labelling what exists
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域形容模型能创造新的文本、图像或音频，而不只是给已有内容分类
senses.example: A generative model can draft a picture from a written prompt.
senses.exampleCN: 生成模型能根据文字提示画出一幅图。
senses.why: The newest use keeps the old image: a model that begets new samples rather than merely sorting them.
senses.whyCN: 最新的用法保留了旧意象：模型「生出」新样本，而不只是给已有样本分类。

intro.en: Generative comes from Latin generare, to beget, through the English verb generate and the adjective suffix -ive.
intro.cn: generative 来自拉丁语 generare（生育），经英语动词 generate 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成。

items.en: Gignere means to beget or bring forth.
items.cn: gignere 意为生育、产生。

items.en: Generare means to beget or produce.
items.cn: generare 意为生育、产生。

items.en: Generativus, a later adjective, means having the power to produce.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语形容词 generativus 意为有产生能力的。

items.en: The verb generate enters English for producing or bringing forth.
items.cn: 动词 generate 在十六世纪进入英语，表示产生或带来。

items.en: Generative enters English in the seventeenth century as a word for producing.
items.cn: generative 在十七世纪进入英语，表示有产生能力的。

items.en: Linguistics and computing give it two technical homes.
items.cn: 语言学与计算机科学给了它两个技术领域。

note.en: Generative joins the birth family: generate, generation, and generator all keep the Latin sense of bringing forth.
note.cn: generative 属于「生育」词族：generate、generation 与 generator 都保留拉丁语「产生」之义。

entries.definition: to produce or create something
entries.definitionCN: 产生；生成，是本词的动词词基

entries.definition: the act of producing, or all people born around the same time
entries.definitionCN: 产生；一代人，由 generate 加名词后缀构成

entries.definition: a machine or program that produces something
entries.definitionCN: 发电机；生成器，词根同为 generare（产生）

entries.definition: able to produce original ideas or works
entries.definitionCN: 有创造力的

entries.definition: producing a lot of results
entries.definitionCN: 多产的；有成效的

entries.definition: able to produce young or crops
entries.definitionCN: 能生育的；肥沃的

normalIntro.en: Generative carries the image of birth: something in it has the power to bring forth more of its kind.
normalIntro.cn: generative 带着「生育」的意象：它内部有一种生出同类新东西的力量。

normal.en: Generate is the verb, generation the act, generative the quality.
normal.cn: generate 是动词，generation 是行为，generative 是性质。

normal.en: Generative AI produces new text or images instead of copying old ones.
normal.cn: 生成式人工智能产出新的文字或图像，而不是复制旧内容。

normal.en: A generative grammar is a rule system that can produce every sentence.
normal.cn: 生成语法是一套能产出所有句子的规则系统。

normal.en: Fertile soil and generative minds both keep producing new growth.
normal.cn: 肥沃的土壤与有生成力的头脑都在不断产出新的生长。

normal.en: Compare creative: creative stresses originality, generative stresses the power to produce.
normal.cn: 对比 creative：creative 强调原创，generative 强调产出的能力。

abstract.en: Picture a seed splitting open and a green shoot pushing out.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子裂开，一截绿芽顶出来。

abstract.en: See a fountain that keeps throwing up new shapes from the same source.
abstract.cn: 想象一股喷泉从同一个源头不断抛出新的形状。

abstract.en: Imagine a small rulebook that can write an endless supply of sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一本小规则书能写出无穷无尽的句子。

examples.en: The generative power of the seed lies in its ability to start a whole plant.
examples.cn: 种子的生成力在于它能长成一整株植物。

examples.en: Linguists use generative rules to explain how children create sentences they have never heard.
examples.cn: 语言学家用生成规则解释儿童如何造出从未听过的句子。

examples.en: A generative model produced a new image from a short description.
examples.cn: 一个生成模型根据简短描述产出了一幅新图像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「真能生」——generate 是「产生」，后缀 -ive 让这个词听起来像「真能生」的；谐音联想，非词源。

root: 拉丁语 gignere（生育）→ generare（产生）→ 后期拉丁语 generativus → 法语 generatif → 英语 generative，核心义「有生出新东西的能力」。

sensesIntro.en: Generative moves from living things to minds, then to rule systems, and finally to machines that produce new samples.
sensesIntro.cn: generative 从生物体走到头脑，再走到规则系统，最后走到产出新样本的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed splitting open to release a new shoot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒种子裂开，放出新芽。

branches.en: The biological sense is the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 生物生殖义是最早的层次。

branches.en: The creative sense moves the power from bodies to minds.
branches.cn: 创造义把这种力量从身体移到头脑。

branches.en: The linguistic sense makes rules the source of sentences.
branches.cn: 语言学义项让规则成为句子的来源。

branches.en: The computing sense makes models the source of new samples.
branches.cn: 计算机义项让模型成为新样本的来源。

branches.en: Both a seed and an idea are generative because each can start something new.
branches.cn: 种子与想法都具有生成力，因为二者都能开启新事物。

intro.en: Generative is built on the Latin birth root gen-, through generate and the adjective suffix -ive.
intro.cn: generative 建立在拉丁语「生育」词根 gen- 上，经 generate 与形容词后缀 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin gignere and generare both mean to beget, and generativus means able to produce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gignere 与 generare 都意为生育，generativus 意为有产生能力的。

items.example: Gignere is the oldest birth root of the family.
items.exampleCN: gignere 是这个词族最古老的「生育」词根。

items.example: Genus is a close relative of the birth root.
items.exampleCN: genus 与「生育」词根是近亲。

items.example: Generare feeds the English verb generate.
items.exampleCN: generare 滋养出英语动词 generate。

items.example: Generativus is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: generativus 是直接的拉丁语祖先。

items.example: Generate is the verb at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: generate 是这个词族的中心动词。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ive forms generative from generate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 由 generate 构成 generative。

items.example: Generation names the act of producing.
items.exampleCN: generation 指产生的行为。

items.example: Generator adds -or to the verb.
items.exampleCN: generator 在动词后加 -or。

items.example: Generative is the adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: generative 是这个词族的形容词。

items.example: Regenerate adds re- to the same root.
items.exampleCN: regenerate 在同一词根前加 re-。

definition_zh: 亲切的；和蔼的；宜人的
definition_en: friendly and cheerful, or pleasantly mild
core_image: 冬日壁炉边，主人笑着为客人添茶
scene: 小旅馆的老板一边笑着招呼客人，一边往壁炉里添柴。The guesthouse owner gave every traveller a genial welcome and a seat by the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 genial 是「亲切友好的」（第 1 个义项：待人热情和善）；句意：旅馆老板给每位旅客亲切的欢迎，并请他们坐到炉火旁。

derivatives.zh: 亲切；和蔼，由 genial 加 -ity 构成
亲切地；和蔼地，由 genial 加 -ly 构成
意气相投的；宜人的，由 con- 加 genial 构成

senses.title: Friendly and warm in manner
senses.definition: kind, cheerful, and easy to talk to
senses.definitionCN: 和善、愉快，容易交谈的
senses.example: Our genial guide made the long walk feel short.
senses.exampleCN: 我们和蔼的向导让漫长的步行变得短暂。
senses.why: Latin genialis first described the festive warmth of a birthday or a feast, so the word kept that social glow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 genialis 最初描述生日或宴席上的喜庆暖意，因此这个词保留了那种社交温度。

senses.title: Pleasantly mild
senses.definition: of weather or a place, pleasantly warm and mild rather than harsh
senses.definitionCN: 指天气或地方温和舒适，而不严酷
senses.example: The valley has a genial climate that suits vines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷气候宜人，适合种葡萄。
senses.why: A festive, welcoming atmosphere can also belong to a place, so genial came to describe mild weather and comfortable surroundings.
senses.whyCN: 喜庆、宜人的气氛也可以属于一个地方，于是 genial 也用来形容温和的天气与舒适的环境。

senses.title: Cheerful and festive in old use
senses.definition: in older literary use, joyful and festive, as of a celebration
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文学用法中形容欢快喜庆，如庆典一般
senses.example: The hall was filled with genial music and laughter.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里满是欢快的音乐与笑声。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is the joy of a feast, and this festive sense survives in literary description.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的层次是宴席的欢乐，这一喜庆义项仍留在文学描写中。

intro.en: Genial comes from Latin genialis, festive or pleasant, which grew out of genius, the spirit of a place or a family.
intro.cn: genial 来自拉丁语 genialis（喜庆的、愉快的），而 genialis 又由 genius（地方或家族的守护灵）发展而来。

items.en: Gignere means to beget, the root behind genius and genus.
items.cn: gignere 意为生育，是 genius 与 genus 共同的词根。

items.en: Genius names the guardian spirit of a person, family, or place.
items.cn: genius 指人、家族或地方的守护灵。

items.en: Genialis means festive, jovial, or belonging to a birthday.
items.cn: genialis 意为喜庆的、欢乐的，或与生日有关的。

items.en: French genial carries the festive sense into later use.
items.cn: 法语 genial 把喜庆之义带入后世用法。

items.en: English first uses genial for marriage and festivity, then for a warm manner.
items.cn: 英语先用 genial 表示婚姻与喜庆，后表示温暖的态度。

items.en: The weather sense of genial settles in by the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，genial 表示气候宜人的义项稳定下来。

note.en: Genial belongs to the genius family: geniality, genially, and congenial all keep a glow of shared warmth.
note.cn: genial 属于 genius 词族：geniality、genially 与 congenial 都保留共享暖意的感觉。

entries.definition: pleasant because it suits your nature
entries.definitionCN: 意气相投的；宜人的，由 con- 加 genial 构成

entries.definition: the quality of being friendly and cheerful
entries.definitionCN: 亲切；和蔼，由 genial 加名词后缀构成

entries.definition: an unusually great natural ability, or a person who has it
entries.definitionCN: 天才；天赋，与 genial 同源于拉丁语 genius

entries.definition: behaving in a kind and pleasant way
entries.definitionCN: 友好的

entries.definition: warm and sincere in manner
entries.definitionCN: 热诚的；亲切的（正式）

entries.definition: easy to approach and pleasant to talk to
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；易于交谈的（正式）

normalIntro.en: Genial is the glow of a shared feast: a birthday spirit made into a manner.
normalIntro.cn: genial 是共享宴席的暖意：把生日的喜庆精灵变成一种待人的态度。

normal.en: Genius is the spirit behind genial: to be genial is to bring that warmth to others.
normal.cn: genius 是 genial 背后的精灵：待人 genial，就是把那种暖意带给别人。

normal.en: A genial host makes guests feel at home within a minute.
normal.cn: genial 的主人能让客人在一分钟内感到自在。

normal.en: Geniality is the noun, genially the adverb, both keeping the friendly glow.
normal.cn: geniality 是名词，genially 是副词，二者都保留了亲切的暖意。

normal.en: Congenial places and people both suit your nature.
normal.cn: congenial 的地方与人，都合你的性情。

normal.en: Compare friendly: friendly is plain and common, genial is warmer and slightly literary.
normal.cn: 对比 friendly：friendly 平实常见，genial 更温暖、略偏书面。

abstract.en: Picture an old innkeeper pulling a chair closer to the fire for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老店主把椅子拉近炉火，请客人坐下。

abstract.en: See a late spring afternoon when the air is soft and nobody hurries.
abstract.cn: 想象晚春的午后，空气柔和，没有人匆忙。

abstract.en: Hear laughter and a small band at a birthday feast.
abstract.cn: 想象生日宴上传来笑声与一支小乐队的演奏。

examples.en: The genial professor remembered every student by name.
examples.cn: 这位和蔼的教授记得每个学生的名字。

examples.en: We spent a genial afternoon on the sunny terrace.
examples.cn: 我们在阳光明媚的露台上度过了一个惬意的下午。

examples.en: Her genial manner hides a very sharp mind.
examples.cn: 她和蔼的举止之下藏着非常敏锐的头脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「见您乐」——genial 读音近「见您乐」，见谁都乐，便是亲切和蔼；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gignere（生育）→ genius（守护灵、天性）→ genialis（喜庆的、愉快的）→ 英语 genial，核心义「带着喜庆暖意的亲切」。

sensesIntro.en: Genial begins with the warmth of a feast, moves to the warmth of a person, and then to the mildness of a place.
sensesIntro.cn: genial 从宴席的暖意开始，转到人的温暖，再转到地方的温和。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a host smiling by a fire and pouring tea for a guest.
core.cn: 核心意象：主人在炉火旁笑着为客人倒茶。

branches.en: The friendly manner is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 亲切的态度是日常义项。

branches.en: The mild weather sense moves the warmth outdoors.
branches.cn: 气候温和义把暖意移到户外。

branches.en: The festive sense is the oldest literary layer.
branches.cn: 喜庆义是最早的文学层次。

branches.en: A genial host and a genial climate both make people linger.
branches.cn: 和蔼的主人与宜人的气候都让人愿意多待。

branches.en: The warmth of a feast became the warmth of a person.
branches.cn: 宴席的暖意变成了人的暖意。

intro.en: Genial grows from the Latin root gen- for begetting, through genius and genialis.
intro.cn: genial 从表示「生育」的拉丁词根 gen- 生长出来，经 genius 与 genialis 而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin genius means a guardian spirit, and genialis means festive or pleasant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genius 意为守护灵，genialis 意为喜庆的、愉快的。

items.example: Gignere is the birth root behind the family.
items.exampleCN: gignere 是这个词族背后的「生育」词根。

items.example: Genus shares the same root as genius.
items.exampleCN: genus 与 genius 共享同一词根。

items.example: Genius is the spirit that gives genial its warmth.
items.exampleCN: genius 是赋予 genial 暖意的精灵。

items.example: Genialis is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: genialis 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Genial is the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: genial 是英语形容词。

items.example: Geniality adds -ity to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: geniality 在形容词后加 -ity。

items.example: Genially adds -ly to the adjective.
items.exampleCN: genially 在形容词后加 -ly。

items.example: Congenial adds con- to genial.
items.exampleCN: congenial 在 genial 前加 con-。

items.example: The suffix -al forms genial from genius.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 由 genius 构成 genial。

items.example: The prefix con- builds congenial.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 构成 congenial。

definition_zh: 体裁；类型；（艺术）风俗画
definition_en: a category of artistic work, or a kind of thing in general
core_image: 书店里一排书架，按侦探、爱情、科幻分门别类
scene: 书店老板把新到的小说按侦探、爱情、科幻分别放上不同的书架。The bookseller sorted the new novels onto separate shelves by genre, one for crime, one for romance, one for science fiction.
sceneCN: 这里 genre 是「体裁；类型」（第 1 个义项：文艺作品的分类）；句意：书店老板把新到的小说按体裁分别放上不同的书架。

derivatives.zh: 子类型；次类型，由 sub- 加 genre 构成
打破类型界限的，由 genre 与 bending 复合而成
特定类型的，由 genre 与 specific 复合而成

senses.title: A category of art
senses.definition: a class or category of literature, music, film, or art, marked by shared style and conventions
senses.definitionCN: 文学、音乐、电影或艺术的类别，以共同的风格与惯例为标志
senses.example: Crime fiction is a genre with strict reader expectations.
senses.exampleCN: 犯罪小说是一种读者期待很明确的体裁。
senses.why: Genre is Latin genus borrowed through French, so a genre is simply a kind, applied to works of art.
senses.whyCN: genre 是经法语借入的拉丁语 genus（种类），所以一种 genre 就是一种类别，用在艺术作品上。

senses.title: A kind of thing in general
senses.definition: a broad type or category of anything, not only art
senses.definitionCN: 任何事物的大类，不限于艺术作品
senses.example: This kind of app has become a genre of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 这类应用已经自成一个类型。
senses.why: Once the word names a class of works, it easily widens to name any recognisable class of things.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能命名一类作品，就很容易扩展到命名任何可辨认的事物类别。

senses.title: Commercial categories of film and fiction
senses.definition: a style of popular film or fiction built on familiar formulas, such as horror, western, or romantic comedy
senses.definitionCN: 通俗电影或小说中依靠熟悉套路的样式，如恐怖片、西部片或爱情喜剧
senses.example: The studio mainly produces genre films for streaming platforms.
senses.exampleCN: 这家制片厂主要为流媒体平台制作类型片。
senses.why: Popular cinema turned artistic kinds into market labels, and the word followed the money.
senses.whyCN: 大众电影把艺术类别变成市场标签，这个词也跟着商业走。

senses.title: Everyday-life painting
senses.definition: in art history, painting that shows ordinary domestic or street life rather than heroic or religious subjects
senses.definitionCN: 艺术史中描绘日常家庭或街头生活、而非英雄或宗教题材的绘画
senses.example: The museum owns a fine genre scene of a village market.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆藏有一幅描绘乡村集市的精美风俗画。
senses.why: French art criticism used genre for a low, everyday category of painting, and that specialist sense stayed.
senses.whyCN: 法国艺术评论用 genre 指一类描绘日常生活的「低级」绘画，这一专门义项保留了下来。

intro.en: Genre is French for kind, and French took it from Latin genus, the same class word behind general and generate.
intro.cn: genre 是法语中表示「种类」的词，法语又从拉丁语 genus 借来，而 general 与 generate 也出自这个词。

items.en: Genus means kind, sort, or class.
items.cn: genus 意为种类、类别。

items.en: Generis is the genitive form that shows the stem gener-.
items.cn: 属格形式 generis 显示出词干 gener-。

items.en: Gendre names a kind or a family line.
items.cn: gendre 指种类或家族血脉。

items.en: Genre settles into the modern French spelling and keeps the sense of kind.
items.cn: genre 固定为现代法语拼写，保留「种类」之义。

items.en: English borrows genre for the categories of painting and literature.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 genre，指绘画与文学的类别。

items.en: Film studies and publishing turn genre into a familiar label for popular forms.
items.cn: 电影研究与出版业把 genre 变成通俗形式的常用标签。

note.en: Genre is the class word in French dress, close to genus, general, and generic.
note.cn: genre 是穿了法语外衣的「类别」词，与 genus、general 和 generic 相邻。

entries.definition: a rank in biological classification, or a kind
entries.definitionCN: 生物学分类中的「属」；类别，是拉丁语同源词

entries.definition: relating to a whole class rather than a particular member
entries.definitionCN: 通用的；属类的，与 genre 同源于 genus

entries.definition: covering a whole class
entries.definitionCN: 一般的；总体的，同源于拉丁语 genus

entries.definition: a group of things that share a feature
entries.definitionCN: 类别；范畴

entries.definition: a group of people or things with shared qualities
entries.definitionCN: 类型；种类

entries.definition: a distinctive way of doing or making something
entries.definitionCN: 风格；样式

normalIntro.en: Genre is a shelf label: a whole class of works, borrowed from the French word for kind.
normalIntro.cn: genre 是一张贴在书架上的标签：一整类作品，借自法语中表示「种类」的词。

normal.en: Genre and genus are the same Latin class word, one through French, one straight from Latin.
normal.cn: genre 与 genus 是同一个拉丁语「类别」词，一个经法语，一个直接来自拉丁语。

normal.en: A bookshop sorts novels by genre: crime, romance, fantasy, history.
normal.cn: 书店按 genre 给小说分类：犯罪、爱情、奇幻、历史。

normal.en: Genre fiction follows familiar formulas that readers already know.
normal.cn: genre fiction 遵循读者早已熟悉的套路。

normal.en: Genre painting shows ordinary life rather than heroes or saints.
normal.cn: genre painting 画普通人的生活，而不是英雄或圣徒。

normal.en: Compare category: category is neutral and broad, genre is mostly for art and media.
normal.cn: 对比 category：category 中性而宽泛，genre 多用于艺术与媒体。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of shelves, each shelf carrying a different colour label.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面书架，每一层都贴着不同颜色的标签。

abstract.en: See a single book that could sit on three shelves at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书同时可以放在三层书架上。

abstract.en: Imagine a painter setting down a scene of a village market instead of a battle.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家不去画战役，而画下乡村集市的场景。

examples.en: Science fiction is a genre that keeps reinventing itself.
examples.cn: 科幻是一种不断自我更新的体裁。

examples.en: The director mixes genres from horror and comedy in one film.
examples.cn: 这位导演在一部电影里混合了恐怖与喜剧两种类型。

examples.en: Her latest novel crosses the genre line between mystery and romance.
examples.cn: 她的新小说跨过了悬疑与爱情之间的类型界线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「让人热」——某一类作品总能「让人热」起来；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 genus（种类）→ 属格 generis → 古法语 gendre → 法语 genre → 英语 genre，核心义「按共同特征划出的一类作品」。

sensesIntro.en: Genre starts as the class word for art, widens to any kind, then hardens into market labels for popular film and finally names a low everyday category in painting.
sensesIntro.cn: genre 先指艺术的类别词，再扩展到任何种类，然后固化为通俗电影的市场标签，最后在绘画中指日常生活的类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shelf in a bookshop carrying a colour label for a whole kind of book.
core.cn: 核心意象：书店里一层书架，贴着代表一整类书的彩色标签。

branches.en: The artistic category is the core sense.
branches.cn: 艺术分类是核心义项。

branches.en: The general kind sense widens the word.
branches.cn: 泛指种类义扩大了词的范围。

branches.en: The film label sense is commercial.
branches.cn: 类型片义项带商业色彩。

branches.en: The painting sense is the specialist art term.
branches.cn: 风俗画义项是专门的艺术术语。

branches.en: A genre film takes an artistic category and turns it into a selling label.
branches.cn: 类型片把艺术类别变成销售标签。

intro.en: Genre keeps the Latin class root gen- in French dress, with genus and generic as close relatives.
intro.cn: genre 以法语外衣保留拉丁语「类别」词根 gen-，genus 与 generic 是近亲。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus means kind or class, and its genitive generis shows the stem gener-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 genus 意为种类或类别，其属格 generis 显示词干 gener-。

items.example: Genus is the class word at the centre.
items.exampleCN: genus 是居于中心的「类别」词。

items.example: Generis shows the stem that French kept.
items.exampleCN: generis 显示了法语保留的词干。

items.example: Generare belongs to the same class root.
items.exampleCN: generare 属于同一个「类别」词根。

items.example: Gendre is the Old French stage of the word.
items.exampleCN: gendre 是该词的古法语阶段。

items.example: French genre passes the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 genre 把该词传给英语。

items.example: Genre is the English borrowing.
items.exampleCN: genre 是英语借入的形式。

items.example: Generic keeps the Latin class meaning.
items.exampleCN: generic 保留拉丁语「类别」含义。

items.example: General is a close relative of genre.
items.exampleCN: general 是 genre 的近亲。

items.meaning: a smaller category inside a genre
items.example: Subgenre adds sub- to genre.
items.exampleCN: subgenre 在 genre 前加 sub-。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms generic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 generic。

definition_zh: 高贵出身；高尚品格；谦恭有礼；温柔宽厚；慷慨
definition_en: nobility of birth or of character, especially as it shows itself in courtesy and generosity
core_image: 一位贵族脱下外套，披在冻得发抖的陌生人身上
scene: 中世纪的城堡里，诗人借这个词提醒听众：门第并不能决定一个人的价值。True gentilesse, he says, is shown in courtesy rather than in noble blood.
sceneCN: 这里 gentilesse 是「高尚品格」（第 2 个义项：品格上的高贵）；句意：他说，真正的高尚品格体现在谦恭有礼，而不在贵族血统。

pos.zh: 高贵；高尚品格；谦恭（古语、文学用语）

forms.label: 不可数（文学用语，无复数）

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，由古法语 gentil 脱落词尾而来，义为「温柔的；出身高贵的」
gentle 加 -ness 构成的抽象名词，义为「温柔；温和」，逐渐接管了 gentilesse 的日常义
同源集合名词，指低于贵族、高于平民的乡绅阶层
同源形容词，义为「文雅的；上流社会的」，带一点矫饰色彩

senses.title: Noble birth
senses.definition: high rank or ancient lineage inherited by birth
senses.definitionCN: 因出生而拥有的高贵门第或古老家世
senses.example: The old families took pride in their gentilesse.
senses.exampleCN: 那些古老家族以自己的高贵出身自豪。
senses.why: The Latin source names the standing of a clan, so the first sense is rank inherited from a family.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指的是宗族的身份地位，所以第一个义项是从家族继承来的门第。

senses.title: Nobility of character
senses.definition: greatness of spirit shown in conduct rather than in rank
senses.definitionCN: 体现在行为而非门第上的精神高贵
senses.example: Her gentilesse was clear in the way she spoke to servants.
senses.exampleCN: 她对仆人说话的方式清楚显出她的品格高尚。
senses.why: Medieval writers turned the quality inward, arguing that virtue matters more than blood.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪作家把这种品质转向内心，主张德行比血统更重要。

senses.title: Courtesy
senses.definition: polite and respectful behaviour towards other people
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的礼貌与尊重
senses.example: He met the insult with gentilesse, not with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他以谦恭有礼而不是愤怒来回应侮辱。
senses.why: If nobility lives in conduct, the clearest proof is how a person treats other people.
senses.whyCN: 如果高贵存在于行为中，最清楚的证明就是一个人如何对待他人。

senses.title: Gentleness
senses.definition: a mild and kind manner that avoids harshness
senses.definitionCN: 温和仁慈、不尖刻的态度
senses.example: The nurse spoke with a gentilesse that calmed the whole ward.
senses.exampleCN: 护士说话温柔宽厚，让整间病房安静下来。
senses.why: The same French word also carried a milder sense, the one English now keeps in gentle.
senses.whyCN: 同一个法语词也带着更温和的含义，英语如今把它留在 gentle 这个词里。

senses.title: Generosity
senses.definition: readiness to give freely and to forgive easily
senses.definitionCN: 乐于给予、也易于宽恕
senses.example: His gentilesse showed in the land he gave to the village.
senses.exampleCN: 他的慷慨体现在他送给村子的那片土地上。
senses.why: A noble heart was expected to give, so the word extends to open-handedness.
senses.whyCN: 高贵的心被认为应当给予，于是这个词扩展到慷慨大方。

senses.title: Courtly bearing
senses.definition: the polished manners and grace expected in noble company
senses.definitionCN: 在上流圈子里被期待的优雅举止与风度
senses.example: The court was famous for its music and its gentilesse.
senses.exampleCN: 那个宫廷以音乐和文雅风度闻名。
senses.why: Rank brought a style of speech and movement, and the word came to name that style itself.
senses.whyCN: 身份带来一套谈吐与举止的风格，这个词后来也用来指这种风格本身。

intro.en: Gentilesse comes from Old French, from Latin gentilitas, the condition of belonging to a gens, a clan.
intro.cn: gentilesse 来自古法语，源于拉丁语 gentilitas，指属于某一宗族（gens）的身份。

items.en: Gens means a clan or a family group sharing one name.
items.cn: gens 意为宗族，即共享一个名号的家族群体。

items.en: Gentilis means belonging to the same clan, and gentilitas names that bond.
items.cn: gentilis 意为同宗的，gentilitas 指这种族属关系。

items.en: Gentilesse carries the sense of noble birth and noble bearing.
items.cn: gentilesse 承载了高贵出身与高贵风度的含义。

items.en: Chaucer uses gentilesse for nobility of character rather than of blood.
items.cn: 乔叟用 gentilesse 指品格上的高贵，而非血统上的高贵。

items.en: Gentleness takes over the everyday sense, and gentilesse survives as a literary word.
items.cn: gentleness 接管了日常义，gentilesse 则作为文学词留存下来。

note.en: Gentilesse belongs with gentle, gentry, and genteel, and it overlaps with the vocabulary of nobility and courtesy.
note.cn: gentilesse 与 gentle、gentry、genteel 同属一族，并与「高贵」「谦恭」这类词的意义相邻。

entries.definition: mild in nature, or of good family
entries.definitionCN: 温和的；出身良好的（同一拉丁词根）

entries.definition: the class of landowners just below the nobility
entries.definitionCN: 乡绅阶层，地位略低于贵族（同一拉丁词根）

entries.definition: polished and refined in manners
entries.definitionCN: 举止文雅的；上流社会的（同一拉丁词根）

entries.definition: the quality of being noble in rank or in spirit
entries.definitionCN: 高贵，可指门第也可指精神

entries.definition: polite behaviour that shows respect
entries.definitionCN: 谦恭有礼的举止

entries.definition: generosity of spirit, especially towards a rival
entries.definitionCN: 宽宏大量，尤指对对手

normalIntro.en: Gentilesse and gentle grew from the same Latin word for a clan, so the word carries both good birth and a mild heart.
normalIntro.cn: gentilesse 与 gentle 都从拉丁语里表示宗族的同一个词长出来，所以这个词同时带着好门第与温和的心。

normal.en: Gentilesse and gentle share the Latin clan word gens.
normal.cn: gentilesse 与 gentle 共享拉丁语表示宗族的 gens。

normal.en: The French suffix -esse turns an adjective into the name of a quality.
normal.cn: 法语后缀 -esse 把形容词变成表示品质的名词。

normal.en: A person of gentilesse is judged by courtesy, not by a family tree.
normal.cn: 评价一个有 gentilesse 的人看的是谦恭，而不是家谱。

normal.en: Chaucer used the word to ask whether virtue can be inherited.
normal.cn: 乔叟用这个词追问德行是否可以继承。

normal.en: Modern English keeps gentleness for daily use and gentilesse for poetry.
normal.cn: 现代英语把 gentleness 留给日常，把 gentilesse 留给诗歌。

abstract.en: Picture a family crest carved over a door, then a hand wiping tears from a stranger.
abstract.cn: 先想象门楣上刻着家族纹章，再想象一只手替陌生人擦去眼泪。

abstract.en: See a lord kneel down to wash the feet of a traveller.
abstract.cn: 想象一位领主跪下来替旅人洗脚。

abstract.en: Hear a noble voice thank a servant by name.
abstract.cn: 想象一个高贵的声音叫出仆人的名字并向他道谢。

examples.en: The old tale praises gentilesse above wealth.
examples.cn: 这个古老的故事把高尚品格看得比财富更重。

examples.en: She treated every guest with the same gentilesse.
examples.cn: 她对每位客人都同样谦恭有礼。

examples.en: Chaucer asked whether gentilesse could ever be taught.
examples.cn: 乔叟追问高尚品格究竟能否被教会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「真提勒丝」——听起来像「真诚地体贴」，正好是高雅品格的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gens（宗族）→ gentilis（同宗的）→ gentilitas（族属、门第）→ 古法语 gentilesse（高贵出身、高贵风度）→ 英语 gentilesse；核心义从「属于高贵宗族」转向「品格高贵」。

sensesIntro.en: Gentilesse begins as the standing of a noble clan, turns inward to noble character, and then spreads into courtesy, gentleness, generosity, and polished bearing.
sensesIntro.cn: gentilesse 起初指高贵宗族的身份，随后转向内在的高尚品格，再扩展到谦恭、温柔、慷慨与文雅风度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a noble hand giving its cloak to a stranger.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只高贵的手把外套递给陌生人。

branches.en: Noble birth is the oldest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 高贵出身是这个词语义最古老的一层。

branches.en: Noble character is the same quality turned inward.
branches.cn: 高尚品格是同一品质向内转的结果。

branches.en: Courtesy is nobility made visible in speech.
branches.cn: 谦恭有礼是高贵在言语上的可见形式。

branches.en: Gentleness and generosity are the warm sides of one heart.
branches.cn: 温柔与慷慨是同一颗心的温暖两面。

branches.en: Outward rank and polished bearing were once judged together.
branches.cn: 外在身份与文雅风度曾经被放在一起评判。

intro.en: Gentilesse is built on the Latin clan word gens, takes the French quality suffix -esse, and shares a family with gentle, gentry, and genteel.
intro.cn: gentilesse 建立在拉丁语表示宗族的 gens 之上，带上法语表性质的后缀 -esse，并与 gentle、gentry、genteel 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gens names a clan, gentilis means of the same clan, and gentilitas means clan relationship.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gens 指宗族，gentilis 意为同宗的，gentilitas 指族属关系。

items.example: Gens is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: gens 是整个词族的根基。

items.example: Gentilis passes into Old French as gentil.
items.exampleCN: gentilis 进入古法语后写作 gentil。

items.example: Gentilitas supplies the abstract sense of rank.
items.exampleCN: gentilitas 提供了表示身份地位的抽象义。

items.example: Gentil describes both birth and manners.
items.exampleCN: gentil 同时描述出身与举止。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -esse forms gentilesse.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -esse 构成 gentilesse。

items.example: Gentilesse is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: gentilesse 是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.example: Gentle keeps the milder branch of the root.
items.exampleCN: gentle 保留了词根中较温和的一支。

items.example: The suffix -ness builds gentleness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 gentleness。

items.example: Gentleness replaced gentilesse in daily speech.
items.exampleCN: gentleness 在日常语言中取代了 gentilesse。

items.example: Gentry names a social class, not a personal quality.
items.exampleCN: gentry 指一个社会阶层，而非个人品质。

items.example: Genteel adds a note of studied refinement.
items.exampleCN: genteel 带上了刻意讲究的意味。

definition_zh: 长臂猿（亚洲树栖类人猿）
definition_en: a small tailless ape of Asian forests, with very long arms and a loud ringing call
core_image: 一只长臂猿单手挂在树梢，身体像钟摆一样荡出去
scene: 热带雨林的树冠层里，一只动物靠双臂交替抓握，几秒钟就跨过十几米。The gibbon crossed the gap between two trees in three swings.
sceneCN: 这里 gibbon 是「长臂猿」（第 1 个义项：泛指这类树栖类人猿）；句意：那只长臂猿荡了三下，就越过了两棵树之间的空隙。

derivatives.zh: 像长臂猿的，形容手臂极长、善以荡跃移动的样子
合趾猿，长臂猿科中体型最大的一种，词源来自马来语
长臂猿科动物，由科名 Hylobatidae 缩略而来

senses.title: A long-armed forest ape
senses.definition: a small tailless ape that lives in Asian forests and moves by swinging from branch to branch
senses.definitionCN: 生活在亚洲森林、靠双臂荡跃移动的无尾小型猿类
senses.example: A gibbon can clear ten metres in a single swing.
senses.exampleCN: 一只长臂猿荡一下就能跨过十米。
senses.why: The name entered English in the eighteenth century as the everyday word for this one animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字在十八世纪作为这种动物的日常称呼进入英语。

senses.title: A member of the family
senses.definition: any ape of the family Hylobatidae, which also includes the siamang
senses.definitionCN: 长臂猿科的任何一种猿，该科也包括合趾猿
senses.example: The reserve protects several gibbons from different islands.
senses.exampleCN: 保护区保护着来自不同岛屿的好几种长臂猿。
senses.why: Zoology widened the everyday name so that it covers the whole family, not just one kind.
senses.whyCN: 动物学把这个日常名称扩大，使它覆盖整个科，而不只是一种。

senses.title: The narrow genus
senses.definition: the genus Hylobates in particular, as opposed to the larger siamang
senses.definitionCN: 特指长臂猿属，与体型更大的合趾猿相对
senses.example: Some checklists keep gibbon for Hylobates alone.
senses.exampleCN: 有些名录只把 gibbon 留给长臂猿属。
senses.why: Taxonomy sometimes narrows a popular name back to a single genus.
senses.whyCN: 分类学有时会把一个通俗名称收窄回单一属。

senses.title: Used as a modifier
senses.definition: placed before another noun to mean of or about gibbons
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示与长臂猿有关的
senses.example: A gibbon research camp opened beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一座长臂猿研究营地在河边开设起来。
senses.why: English freely turns animal names into modifiers before other nouns.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯把动物名称直接放在其他名词前作定语。

intro.en: Gibbon came into English from French in the eighteenth century, and the further origin of the name is uncertain.
intro.cn: gibbon 在十八世纪从法语进入英语，而这个名称更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: No reliable Asian source word has been established for the name.
items.cn: 目前还没有证实可靠的亚洲语源。

items.en: French naturalists used gibbon for the ape in their accounts.
items.cn: 十八世纪法国博物学家在记述中用 gibbon 称呼这种猿。

items.en: English travel and natural history writing borrowed the French word.
items.cn: 英国的游记与博物学著作借入了这个法语词。

items.en: The word settled as the everyday English name for the long-armed ape.
items.cn: 这个词固定为这种长臂猿在英语里的日常名称。

items.en: Modern biology uses gibbon for one genus and for the whole family.
items.cn: 现代生物学既用它指一个属，也用它指整个科。

note.en: Gibbon is a single animal name, easily confused in spelling with gibbet, gibber, and gibe, and close in meaning to ape and the other great forest primates.
note.cn: gibbon 是一个单一动物名，拼写上容易与 gibbet、gibber、gibe 混淆，意义上则与 ape 及别的森林灵长类相邻。

entries.definition: a wooden frame once used to hang criminals
entries.definitionCN: 绞刑架；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to speak fast in a way that is hard to understand
entries.definitionCN: 急促含混地说；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a mocking remark
entries.definitionCN: 嘲弄的话；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a primate without a tail, such as a chimpanzee
entries.definitionCN: 猿，无尾的灵长类

entries.definition: a large African ape with dark hair
entries.definitionCN: 黑猩猩，非洲的大型猿类

entries.definition: a large red-haired ape of Sumatra and Borneo
entries.definitionCN: 猩猩，苏门答腊与婆罗洲的大型红毛猿

normalIntro.en: Gibbon is a borrowed animal name, so the best hooks are its French entry, its tailless body, and its arm-over-arm swing.
normalIntro.cn: gibbon 是一个借来的动物名，最好记的钩子是它的法语来源、无尾的身体，以及双臂交替的荡跃。

normal.en: Gibbon reached English through French natural history writing.
normal.cn: gibbon 是经法语博物学著作进入英语的。

normal.en: A gibbon has no tail, which sets it apart from most monkeys.
normal.cn: 长臂猿没有尾巴，这一点让它与大多数猴子区别开。

normal.en: A gibbon moves by brachiation, swinging arm over arm through the canopy.
normal.cn: 长臂猿靠臂行移动，在树冠间双臂交替荡跃。

normal.en: The plural is simply gibbons.
normal.cn: 复数形式就是 gibbons。

normal.en: Keep gibbon apart from gibbet: one is an ape, the other a gallows.
normal.cn: 把 gibbon 和 gibbet 分开：一个是猿，一个是绞刑架。

abstract.en: Picture a long body flying between two trunks, arms first.
abstract.cn: 想象一具修长的身体在两棵树干之间飞过，双臂伸在前面。

abstract.en: Imagine an ape family tree with one long branch marked gibbon.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵猿类家系树，上面有一根长枝标着 gibbon。

abstract.en: See a checklist with a single genus name circled in ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张名录，上面有一个属名被墨水圈了出来。

examples.en: The gibbon sings at dawn to mark the boundaries of its territory.
examples.cn: 长臂猿在黎明鸣唱，标记领地的边界。

examples.en: A young gibbon learns to swing before it is a year old.
examples.cn: 幼年长臂猿不到一岁就学会荡跃。

examples.en: Scientists counted fewer gibbons in the reserve than last year.
examples.cn: 科学家在保护区统计到的长臂猿比去年少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「机绷」——手臂一绷紧就弹出去，正像长臂猿荡树的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 词源不确定：一般认为是法语 gibbon 借入英语，可能源自东南亚某地语言，但未能证实；核心义一直是「亚洲的长臂猿」。

sensesIntro.en: Gibbon starts as the everyday name of one Asian ape, then widens to the whole family in zoology, narrows again to a single genus, and finally works as a noun modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: gibbon 起初是某一种亚洲猿的日常名称，在动物学里扩大为整个科，又被收窄为单一属，最后还用作名词定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body swinging from branch to branch by its arms.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体靠双臂从一根树枝荡到另一根。

branches.en: The everyday animal name is the base sense.
branches.cn: 日常动物名是这个词的基础义。

branches.en: The family sense gathers every long-armed kind together.
branches.cn: 科级义把所有长臂的种类归到一起。

branches.en: The genus sense narrows to one branch of that family.
branches.cn: 属级义收窄到那个科里的一个分支。

branches.en: The modifier use simply puts the animal name before another noun.
branches.cn: 定语用法只是把这个动物名放到另一个名词前面。

branches.en: Popular and technical use differ only in how wide the name reaches.
branches.cn: 通俗用法与技术用法的差别，只在这个名称覆盖的范围。

intro.en: Gibbon takes no living English affixes; its family is built instead from compounds, the scientific family name, and the borrowed word siamang.
intro.cn: gibbon 在现代英语里不接活性词缀，它的词族由复合词、科名与借词 siamang 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor or Latin relative for gibbon, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: gibbon 没有拉丁语祖先，也没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: Gibbon is the base word of the family.
items.exampleCN: gibbon 是这个词族的基础词。

items.example: The plural takes a simple -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数只加一个 -s。

items.example: Gibbon-like arms reach far across the gap.
items.exampleCN: 长臂猿般的手臂能伸过很宽的空隙。

items.example: The suffix -like forms gibbon-like.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -like 构成 gibbon-like。

items.meaningCN: 合趾猿，体型最大的长臂猿
items.example: Siamang names a close relative, not a synonym.
items.exampleCN: siamang 指一个近亲，而不是同义词。

items.example: Hylobates appears in technical writing on gibbons.
items.exampleCN: 长臂猿属的学名出现在关于长臂猿的技术文献里。

items.example: Hylobatidae gathers every gibbon kind.
items.exampleCN: 长臂猿科的科名把各种长臂猿归在一起。

items.meaningCN: 动物分类中表示「科」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -idae marks a family in zoology.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -idae 在动物学中标记一个科。

items.meaning: a member of the gibbon family
items.example: Hylobatid is the short technical noun.
items.exampleCN: hylobatid 是简短的技术名词。

items.meaningCN: 臂行，双臂交替在树间荡跃
items.example: Brachiation is how a gibbon travels.
items.exampleCN: 臂行是长臂猿移动的方式。

definition_zh: 巨大的；庞大的；极大的
definition_en: extremely large in size, in scale, or in degree
core_image: 一只巨人的手掌托起整座小屋
scene: 展厅里那尊雕像高过屋顶，观众要一直退到墙边才看得全。A gigantic statue fills the hall, and visitors must step back to see its head.
sceneCN: 这里 gigantic 是「体积巨大」（第 1 个义项：物体的尺寸极大）；句意：一尊巨大的雕像占满大厅，观众得后退才能看见它的头部。

derivatives.zh: 巨人；庞然大物，也可作形容词表示巨大的
gigantic 加 -ally 构成的副词，义为「巨大地」
女巨人，由 giant 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成
经法语 -esque 构成的形容词，义为「巨人般的；庞大得夸张的」

senses.title: Huge in physical size
senses.definition: of a physical size far beyond what is normal
senses.definitionCN: 物理尺寸远超寻常
senses.example: A gigantic boulder blocked the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 一块巨大的巨石堵住了山路。
senses.why: Greek gigas names a giant of myth, so the adjective begins with the size of a body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 gigas 指神话中的巨人，所以这个形容词从身体的尺寸开始。

senses.title: Huge in scale
senses.definition: of an extent or scale that dwarfs ordinary examples
senses.definitionCN: 范围或规模使寻常事物显得渺小
senses.example: The dam was a gigantic engineering project.
senses.exampleCN: 那座大坝是一项规模宏大的工程。
senses.why: From one body the word extends to whole works and systems built by many hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一具身体扩展到众人建造的整套工程与体系。

senses.title: Huge in amount
senses.definition: of a number or sum that is hard to take in
senses.definitionCN: 数目或金额大得难以想象
senses.example: The company reported a gigantic loss last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年报告了巨额亏损。
senses.why: Counting large sums borrows the giant image, since big money is pictured as big matter.
senses.whyCN: 计算大笔金额时借用了巨人的意象，因为大钱在心里就是一大堆东西。

senses.title: Huge in degree
senses.definition: of an effort, feeling, or difference that is extreme
senses.definitionCN: 努力、情感或差异达到极端
senses.example: They made a gigantic effort to finish before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 他们付出巨大努力，想在天黑前完成。
senses.why: Effort and feeling are measured like bodies, so the giant image carries straight over.
senses.whyCN: 努力与情感被当作有体量的东西来衡量，巨人的意象于是直接搬了过来。

senses.title: Of a very tall person
senses.definition: of a person, very tall and heavily built
senses.definitionCN: 指人身材极高、体格魁梧
senses.example: A gigantic doorkeeper stood beside the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 门旁站着一个身材高大的门房。
senses.why: The oldest use describes giant-like people, and that bodily sense never disappeared.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法描述像巨人的人，这层身体义从未消失。

intro.en: Gigantic goes back through Latin giganticus to Greek gigas, the giant of myth, a word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: gigantic 经拉丁语 giganticus 上溯到希腊语 gigas（神话中的巨人），该词来源不确定。

items.en: Gigas means a giant, with the stem gigant- in the other cases.
items.cn: gigas 意为巨人，其他格使用词干 gigant-。

items.en: The origin of gigas is uncertain and is often called Pre-Greek.
items.cn: gigas 的来源不确定，通常被视为前希腊语词。

items.en: Giganticus means of the giants, formed from the Greek stem.
items.cn: giganticus 意为巨人的，由希腊语词干构成。

items.en: Gigantic enters English as a literary adjective for giant-like things.
items.cn: gigantic 在十七世纪作为文学形容词进入英语，形容像巨人的事物。

items.en: Modern use widens it from bodies to projects, sums, and efforts.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从身体扩展到工程、金额与努力。

note.en: Gigantic belongs to the giant family, and its nearest neighbours are the scale adjectives enormous, colossal, and mammoth.
note.cn: gigantic 属于「巨人」词族，最近的邻居是 enormous、colossal、mammoth 这一组表示尺度的形容词。

entries.definition: an imaginary being of great size, or something very large
entries.definitionCN: 巨人；庞然大物（同一希腊词根）

entries.definition: abnormally great growth or size
entries.definitionCN: 巨人症；巨大化（同一希腊词根）

entries.definition: huge in an exaggerated, theatrical way
entries.definitionCN: 庞大得夸张的（同一希腊词根，经法语构成）

entries.definition: very large indeed
entries.definitionCN: 极大的；巨大的

entries.definition: of the size of a colossal statue
entries.definitionCN: 巨像般的；巨大的

entries.definition: huge, like the extinct elephant
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的，像已灭绝的猛犸象

normalIntro.en: Gigantic carries the Greek giant gigas inside it, so the word is a body picture before it is a measurement.
normalIntro.cn: gigantic 里面藏着希腊语的巨人 gigas，所以这个词先是身体的画面，然后才是度量。

normal.en: The stem gigant- is the Greek word for a giant.
normal.cn: 词干 gigant- 就是希腊语里表示巨人的词。

normal.en: Latin giganticus simply means of the giants.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 giganticus 的意思就是「巨人的」。

normal.en: The ending -ic makes an adjective of quality, as in gigantic.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ic 构成表示性质的形容词，gigantic 正是如此。

normal.en: Gigantic describes size, scale, amount, and degree, not only bodies.
normal.cn: gigantic 可以形容体积、规模、数量与程度，不只是身体。

normal.en: For a plain comparison, use more gigantic and most gigantic.
normal.cn: 需要比较时用 more gigantic 与 most gigantic。

abstract.en: Picture a giant hand holding a house the way a child holds a toy.
abstract.cn: 想象一只巨人的手托起一座小屋，像孩子拿玩具那样。

abstract.en: Imagine a dam so wide that a whole town could sit on its top.
abstract.cn: 想象一座大坝宽得能在坝顶安置整个小镇。

abstract.en: Think of a number so large that it stops meaning anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字大到失去意义。

examples.en: A gigantic wave swept over the harbour wall.
examples.cn: 一个巨浪越过了港口的防波堤。

examples.en: Rebuilding the bridge was a gigantic task for the small town.
examples.cn: 重建这座桥对小镇来说是一项艰巨的任务。

examples.en: The two plans differ by a gigantic margin.
examples.cn: 两个方案之间存在巨大的差距。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吉甘铁克」——听起来像「极巨大的铁壳」，正是庞然大物的感觉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 gigas（巨人，属格 gigant-，来源不确定，常被视为前希腊语词）→ 拉丁语 giganticus（巨人的）→ 英语 gigantic；核心义「像巨人一样的体量」。

sensesIntro.en: Gigantic starts from the body of a mythic giant, then stretches to great works, to huge sums, to extreme effort, and back to very tall people.
sensesIntro.cn: gigantic 从神话巨人的身体出发，扩展到宏大的工程、庞大的金额、极端的努力，又回到身材极高的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a giant hand lifting a whole house.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只巨手托起整座房子。

branches.en: Physical size is the first and clearest sense.
branches.cn: 物理尺寸是最早也最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Scale widens the body image to whole structures.
branches.cn: 规模义把身体的意象扩大到整座建筑。

branches.en: Amount treats big money as big matter.
branches.cn: 数量义把大笔金钱当成大堆物质。

branches.en: Degree applies the same bigness to effort and feeling.
branches.cn: 程度义把同一种「大」用在努力与情感上。

branches.en: Both the statue and the tall doorkeeper are giant-like bodies.
branches.cn: 雕像与高大的门房都是巨人般的身体。

intro.en: Gigantic is built from the Greek giant word gigas, its stem gigant-, the Latin adjective ending, and the English suffix -ic.
intro.cn: gigantic 由希腊语表示巨人的 gigas、其词干 gigant-、拉丁形容词词尾以及英语后缀 -ic 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed gigas from Greek and formed giganticus, the direct parent of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借来 gigas，并构成 giganticus，它正是英语这个形容词的直接来源。

items.example: Gigas names the giant of myth.
items.exampleCN: gigas 指神话中的巨人。

items.example: The stem gigant- carries the meaning into Latin.
items.exampleCN: 词干 gigant- 把词义带进拉丁语。

items.example: Giganticus is the direct parent of gigantic.
items.exampleCN: giganticus 是 gigantic 的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ic builds the adjective gigantic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成形容词 gigantic。

items.example: Gigantic keeps the whole giant image.
items.exampleCN: gigantic 保留了完整的巨人意象。

items.example: Giant is the shorter everyday relative.
items.exampleCN: giant 是更短的日常同族词。

items.example: The suffix -ess forms giantess.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ess 构成 giantess。

items.example: Giantess is giant plus a feminine ending.
items.exampleCN: giantess 是 giant 加阴性词尾。

items.example: Gigantically is the adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: gigantically 是方式副词。

items.example: The suffix -esque forms gigantesque.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -esque 构成 gigantesque。

definition_zh: 巨人症；巨大化；巨型化
definition_en: abnormally great growth or size, especially the hormonal disorder that makes a person grow far too tall
core_image: 一双还在变大的鞋，鞋柜里上一双只穿了半年
scene: 少年一年里长了半个头，鞋码换了三次，医生怀疑问题出在脑部的腺体。The clinic tests children for gigantism when their growth refuses to stop.
sceneCN: 这里 gigantism 是「巨人症」（第 1 个义项：生长激素过量导致的异常高大）；句意：当孩子的生长停不下来时，诊所会为他做巨人症检查。

forms.label: 不可数（医学与生物学用语，无复数）

derivatives.zh: 巨人；庞然大物，gigantism 的词根在日常英语里的代表词
巨大的；庞大的，同词根的形容词
巨大地，由 gigantic 加 -ally 构成

senses.title: The hormonal disorder
senses.definition: a condition caused by excess growth hormone before adult height is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在成年身高定型前，生长激素过多导致的一种病症
senses.example: Untreated gigantism can leave a patient far above normal height.
senses.exampleCN: 未经治疗的巨人症会让患者的身高远超常人。
senses.why: The Greek giant supplies the image, and the medical suffix turns it into the name of a disease.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语的巨人提供意象，医学后缀把它变成一种疾病的名称。

senses.title: Excessive growth in other species
senses.definition: unusually large growth in a plant or animal group, often on islands
senses.definitionCN: 某一动植物类群的异常增大，常见于岛屿环境
senses.example: Island gigantism produced beetles as large as a fist.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿巨大化造就了拳头大的甲虫。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the medical word for any group that evolves a far larger body.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用了这个医学词，指任何演化出远大体型的类群。

senses.title: Runaway growth of institutions
senses.definition: the excessive growth of an organization or system beyond a workable size
senses.definitionCN: 组织或体系膨胀到难以运作的规模
senses.example: Critics warn of corporate gigantism in the media industry.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者警告传媒业出现企业巨型化。
senses.why: Once a word names excessive size, it can be applied to bodies of any kind, including companies.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示过度的庞大，就能用在任何「体」上，包括公司。

senses.title: The state of being gigantic
senses.definition: great size treated as a quality or condition in its own right
senses.definitionCN: 把巨大的体量本身当作一种性质或状态
senses.example: The sculpture impresses by sheer gigantism rather than by detail.
senses.exampleCN: 那座雕塑靠纯粹的庞大体量而不是细节打动人。
senses.why: The suffix -ism can name a state as well as a disease, so the word also means sheer bigness.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 既能指病症，也能指状态，所以这个词也指纯粹的庞大。

intro.en: Gigantism joins the Greek stem gigant-, from gigas, a giant, to the suffix -ism, and it was coined in English medical writing.
intro.cn: gigantism 把希腊语词干 gigant-（来自 gigas，巨人）与后缀 -ism 结合，是英语医学写作中造出的词。

items.en: Gigas means a giant, and its stem is gigant-.
items.cn: gigas 意为巨人，其词干为 gigant-。

items.en: The suffix -ismos names a condition, practice, or doctrine.
items.cn: 后缀 -ismos 表示状态、做法或学说。

items.en: Latin keeps the stem gigant- in giganticus and related words.
items.cn: 拉丁语在 giganticus 等相关词中保留了词干 gigant-。

items.en: Medical writers coin gigantism for growth that does not stop.
items.cn: 医学作者造出 gigantism，指停不下来的生长。

items.en: Biology and social criticism extend it to island species and to huge institutions.
items.cn: 生物学与社会批评把它扩展到岛屿物种与庞大机构。

note.en: Gigantism sits inside the giant family, and its medical neighbours are acromegaly, its opposite dwarfism, and the technical term hypertrophy.
note.cn: gigantism 属于「巨人」词族，医学上的邻居是 acromegaly、反义的 dwarfism，以及技术词 hypertrophy。

entries.definition: extremely large
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的（同一希腊词根）

entries.definition: a huge mythical being, or something very large
entries.definitionCN: 巨人；庞然大物（同一希腊词根）

entries.definition: huge in an exaggerated way
entries.definitionCN: 庞大得夸张的（同一希腊词根）

entries.definition: enlargement of the hands, feet, and face caused by excess growth hormone in adults
entries.definitionCN: 肢端肥大症，成年后生长激素过多导致手足与面部增大

entries.definition: abnormally small growth
entries.definitionCN: 侏儒症，与巨人症相对

entries.definition: the enlargement of an organ or tissue from increased cell size
entries.definitionCN: 肥大，器官或组织因细胞增大而变大

normalIntro.en: Gigantism is the giant stem plus the suffix of conditions, so it names the state of growing like a giant.
normalIntro.cn: gigantism 是「巨人」词干加上表示状态的后缀，所以它指「像巨人一样生长」的状态。

normal.en: The stem gigant- comes straight from the Greek word for a giant.
normal.cn: 词干 gigant- 直接来自希腊语表示巨人的词。

normal.en: The suffix -ism names a condition, as in alcoholism and dwarfism.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ism 表示状态或病症，如 alcoholism 与 dwarfism。

normal.en: Gigantism is usually linked to the pituitary gland.
normal.cn: 巨人症通常与垂体有关。

normal.en: Island gigantism is the biological use of the same word.
normal.cn: 岛屿巨大化是这个词在生物学上的用法。

normal.en: Do not confuse gigantism with gigantic: one is a condition, the other a description.
normal.cn: 不要把 gigantism 与 gigantic 混淆：一个是病症，一个是描述。

abstract.en: Picture a boy at a clinic door, his new shoes already too small.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男孩站在诊所门口，新鞋已经显小。

abstract.en: See a beetle on an island growing as big as a fist.
abstract.cn: 想象岛上的一只甲虫长到拳头那么大。

abstract.en: Think of a company swallowing its rivals until it fills the map.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司吞并对手，直到占满整张地图。

examples.en: Gigantism is usually caused by a tumour on the pituitary gland.
examples.cn: 巨人症通常由垂体上的肿瘤引起。

examples.en: Island gigantism can produce unusually large insects and reptiles.
examples.cn: 岛屿巨大化可以造就异常巨大的昆虫与爬行动物。

examples.en: The historian warns against the gigantism of modern institutions.
examples.cn: 这位历史学家警告现代机构的巨型化倾向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吉甘提兹姆」——听起来像「 gigantic 的极致」，正是身高失控的样子；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 gigas（巨人，词干 gigant-）→ 拉丁语 gigant-（巨人）→ 英语 giant、gigantic，再加后缀 -ism（状态、病症）→ gigantism；核心义「巨人般的过度生长」。

sensesIntro.en: Gigantism begins as a medical name for growth that will not stop, then spreads to oversized species on islands, to swollen institutions, and finally to sheer bigness.
sensesIntro.cn: gigantism 起初是「停不下来的生长」的医学名称，随后扩展到岛屿上的超大物种、膨胀的机构，最后泛指纯粹的庞大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shoes that keep being outgrown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双双很快穿不下的鞋。

branches.en: The medical sense is the historical core.
branches.cn: 医学义是这个词的历史核心。

branches.en: The biological sense applies the same growth to other species.
branches.cn: 生物学义把同一种过度生长用在别的物种上。

branches.en: The institutional sense treats organizations as bodies that can swell.
branches.cn: 机构义把组织当成会膨胀的身体。

branches.en: The state sense is the plainest reading of the suffix.
branches.cn: 状态义是对这个后缀最朴素的读法。

branches.en: Both the patient and the island beetle grow beyond the usual limit.
branches.cn: 病人与岛上的甲虫都长过了通常的限度。

intro.en: Gigantism is the giant stem with the suffix of conditions, -ism, and it shares its family with giant, gigantic, and giantess.
intro.cn: gigantism 是「巨人」词干加上表示状态的后缀 -ism，并与 giant、gigantic、giantess 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek stem gigant- and kept it in giganticus, the adjective behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语接过希腊语词干 gigant-，并把它保留在 giganticus 里，这个形容词是英语词族的前身。

items.example: Gigas is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: gigas 是整个词族的根。

items.example: The stem gigant- joins the suffix -ism.
items.exampleCN: 词干 gigant- 与后缀 -ism 结合。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或做法的后缀
items.example: The Greek suffix -ismos becomes English -ism.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语后缀 -ismos 演变为英语 -ism。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、体系或做法的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ism names conditions such as dwarfism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 用来命名 dwarfism 这类状态。

items.example: Gigantism names the condition itself.
items.exampleCN: gigantism 直接命名这种状态。

items.example: Gigantic is the descriptive relative.
items.exampleCN: gigantic 是描述性的同族形容词。

items.example: Giant is the short everyday word.
items.exampleCN: giant 是简短的日常词。

items.example: Giantess adds a feminine ending.
items.exampleCN: giantess 加上了阴性词尾。

items.example: Acromegaly is the adult counterpart of gigantism.
items.exampleCN: 肢端肥大症是巨人症在成年期的对应病症。

items.example: The suffix -megaly appears in medical terms.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -megaly 出现在医学术语里。

definition_zh: 鳃；菌褶；及耳（液量单位）；溪谷；去鳃
definition_en: the breathing organ of a fish, a plate shaped like it, and several unrelated things that share this spelling
core_image: 鱼头两侧的鳃盖随水流一开一合
scene: 溪边的石板上躺着刚钓上来的鱼，鳃盖还在轻轻开合。The fish was still breathing through its gills when the net lifted it.
sceneCN: 这里 gill 是「鳃」（第 1 个义项：鱼的呼吸器官）；句意：网把鱼提起的时候，它还在用鳃呼吸。

derivatives.zh: 有鳃的；已去鳃的，由 gill 加 -ed 构成
刺网，靠网眼卡住鱼鳃的渔网，由 gill 与 net 复合而成

senses.title: The fish organ
senses.definition: the organ with which a fish takes oxygen from water
senses.definitionCN: 鱼用来从水中获取氧气的器官
senses.example: Water enters the mouth and leaves through the gills.
senses.exampleCN: 水从口进入，再从鳃流出。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense, though the exact origin of the Middle English word is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录以来最早的义项，不过中古英语这个词的确切来源并不确定。

senses.title: A mushroom gill
senses.definition: one of the thin plates under the cap of a mushroom
senses.definitionCN: 蘑菇伞盖下面的一片片薄板
senses.example: The gills under the cap are pale brown.
senses.exampleCN: 伞盖下的菌褶是浅褐色的。
senses.why: The plates look like the ribs of a fish gill, so the name was borrowed by shape.
senses.whyCN: 这些薄板看起来像鱼鳃的鳃条，于是名称按形状被借了过来。

senses.title: A liquid measure
senses.definition: a small unit of liquid equal to a quarter of a pint
senses.definitionCN: 等于四分之一品脱的液体计量单位
senses.example: Add a gill of milk to the batter.
senses.exampleCN: 往面糊里加一及耳牛奶。
senses.why: This is a different word, from Old French, which happened to take the same spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个词，来自古法语，只是碰巧取了相同的拼写。

senses.title: A narrow valley stream
senses.definition: a narrow valley with a stream in it, used in northern England
senses.definitionCN: 英格兰北部指带溪流的狭窄山谷
senses.example: The path follows the gill down to the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 小路沿着溪谷一路下到湖边。
senses.why: This sense comes from Old Norse gil, a ravine, and survives in northern place names.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自古诺斯语 gil（峡谷），并保存在北方的地名里。

senses.title: To gut a fish
senses.definition: to remove the gills of a fish before cooking
senses.definitionCN: 烹饪前把鱼的鳃去掉
senses.example: He gilled and scaled the fish at the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 他在水槽边给鱼去鳃刮鳞。
senses.why: The verb is simply the organ name turned into an action.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把器官名称变成动作。

senses.title: An old word for a girl
senses.definition: an old informal word for a young woman
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中对年轻女子的称呼
senses.example: The old ballad calls her a merry gill.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老歌谣称她为快乐的姑娘。
senses.why: It comes from the woman name Gill, short for Gillian, and it is now obsolete.
senses.whyCN: 它来自女子名 Gill（Gillian 的缩短形式），如今已经废弃。

intro.en: Gill is at least three different words that came to share one spelling: the fish organ, the liquid measure, and the northern ravine.
intro.cn: gill 至少是三个不同的词共用一种拼写：鱼的鳃、液量单位，以及北方的溪谷。

items.en: Gil means a narrow ravine with a stream running through it.
items.cn: gil 意为有溪流穿过的狭窄峡谷。

items.en: Gillo is a small liquid measure, perhaps the source of the French word.
items.cn: gillo 是一种小量器，可能为法语词的前身。

items.en: Gille names a measure of liquid and passes into English.
items.cn: gille 指一种液量，并进入英语。

items.en: Gille is recorded for the fish organ, though its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 gille 已指鱼鳃，但其来源不确定。

items.en: The mushroom plate and the verb to gill extend the shape and the organ.
items.cn: 蘑菇的菌褶义与动词「去鳃」分别延伸了形状与器官这两条线。

note.en: Gill has three unrelated origins under one spelling, so both look-alikes and near meanings need care.
note.cn: gill 在一种拼写下藏着三个互不相关的来源，所以形近词与近义词都要小心区分。

entries.definition: a fishing or hunting guide in Scotland
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰的渔猎向导；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a net that catches fish by their gills
entries.definitionCN: 靠鱼鳃卡住鱼的刺网，由 gill 与 net 复合

entries.definition: covered with a thin layer of gold
entries.definitionCN: 镀金的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a gill, used in zoology
entries.definitionCN: 鳃，动物学中的技术用语

entries.definition: a thin plate, such as a mushroom gill
entries.definitionCN: 薄片，如蘑菇的菌褶

entries.definition: a deep narrow valley
entries.definitionCN: 深而窄的峡谷，与溪谷义相近

normalIntro.en: Gill is a spelling shared by three unrelated words, so learn each sense with its own picture and its own origin.
normalIntro.cn: gill 是三个互不相关的词共用的拼写，所以要为每个义项配上各自的画面与来源。

normal.en: The fish sense is the everyday one: gills take oxygen from water.
normal.cn: 鱼的义项最日常：鳃从水里取氧。

normal.en: The measure gill is pronounced with a soft g, like the name Gill.
normal.cn: 量器义的 gill 读软音 g，和女子名 Gill 同音。

normal.en: The ravine gill comes from Old Norse gil.
normal.cn: 溪谷义的 gill 来自古诺斯语 gil。

normal.en: The plural and the third person both add -s: gills.
normal.cn: 复数与第三人称单数都加 -s，写作 gills。

normal.en: Full to the gills means completely full.
normal.cn: full to the gills 表示塞得满满、饱到极点。

abstract.en: Watch a gill cover open and close with the current.
abstract.cn: 想象鳃盖随着水流一开一合。

abstract.en: Turn a mushroom over and see a stack of thin brown plates.
abstract.cn: 把蘑菇翻过来，看见一叠薄薄的褐色片层。

abstract.en: Picture a cook pouring one small measure into a cup.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师把一小量液体倒进杯子。

examples.en: The fish opened its gills wide in the fresh water.
examples.cn: 那条鱼在清水里把鳃张得很大。

examples.en: Pick mushrooms with pale gills and a dry cap.
examples.cn: 要采菌褶颜色浅、伞盖干燥的蘑菇。

examples.en: The old recipe asks for a gill of cream.
examples.cn: 那份旧食谱要一及耳的奶油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给耳」——鱼用鳃「给」水中的氧气，位置又贴着「耳」后；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 三条来源合成一个拼写：中古英语 gille（鱼鳃，来源不确定）、古法语 gille（液量单位，或上溯晚期拉丁语 gillo）、古诺斯语 gil（峡谷）；核心义各有各的画面，最常用的是「鳃」。

sensesIntro.en: Gill starts with the fish organ, borrows its shape for mushroom plates, keeps a separate French measure, a separate Norse ravine, turns the organ into a verb, and preserves an obsolete word for a girl.
sensesIntro.cn: gill 从鱼的鳃出发，按形状借给蘑菇的菌褶，又各自保留法语量器与诺斯语溪谷两个来源，再把器官名转成动词，并留下一个指少女的废弃旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gill cover opening and closing with the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：鳃盖随水流一开一合。

branches.en: The fish organ is the dominant sense.
branches.cn: 鱼鳃是这个词最主要的义项。

branches.en: The mushroom plate borrows the shape of the organ.
branches.cn: 菌褶义借用了鳃的形状。

branches.en: The measure is a separate French word.
branches.cn: 量器义是一个独立的法语词。

branches.en: The ravine is a separate Norse word.
branches.cn: 溪谷义是一个独立的诺斯语词。

branches.en: The verb simply acts on the organ named by the noun.
branches.cn: 动词只是对名词所指的器官采取动作。

intro.en: Gill has little affix structure of its own; its family comes from the plural, the past form, the compound gillnet, and borrowings from French and Norse.
intro.cn: gill 本身几乎没有词缀结构，它的词族来自复数、过去式、复合词 gillnet，以及法语与诺斯语的借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes gillo, a small measure, and the Latinized Greek branchia, the technical word for a gill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 gillo（小量器）与拉丁化的希腊词 branchia（鳃的技术用语）。

items.meaning: the breathing organ of a fish
items.example: Gill is the base word of the family.
items.exampleCN: gill 是这个词族的基础词。

items.meaning: the pair of organs, or more than one
items.example: The plural is gills, with a simple -s.
items.exampleCN: 复数写作 gills，只加一个 -s。

items.meaning: having gills, or with the gills removed
items.example: Gilled describes a fish or a mushroom.
items.exampleCN: gilled 可形容鱼，也可形容蘑菇。

items.meaningCN: 表示「具有」的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed forms gilled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 gilled。

items.example: Gilling is the work done at the cleaning table.
items.exampleCN: gilling 指在清理台上做的活。

items.meaning: a net that holds fish by the gills
items.example: Gillnet joins gill to net.
items.exampleCN: gillnet 由 gill 与 net 组合而成。

items.example: Gil is the source of the northern gill.
items.exampleCN: gil 是北方溪谷义的来源。

items.example: Gille gives English the measure gill.
items.exampleCN: gille 给英语带来了量器义的 gill。

items.example: Gillo may lie behind the French gille.
items.exampleCN: gillo 可能是法语 gille 的前身。

items.example: Branchia is the formal term in zoology.
items.exampleCN: branchia 是动物学里的正式用语。
